Then, uttering *klīm*, one should display the attracting mudrā (*ākarṣiṇī-mudrā*).
This is the ritual placement for the third enclosure (*tṛtīyāvaraṇanyāsa*).

Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with the mantra: *HAIṂ HAKALĪṂ HASAUḤ SARVASAUBHĀGYADĀYAKACAKRĀYA NAMAḤ*, [one places]: on the right side of the forehead, *KAṂ SARVASAṂKṢOBHIṆĪŚAKTYAI NAMAḤ*;
on the right cheek, *KHAṂ SARVAVIDRĀVIṆĪŚAKTYAI NAMAḤ*; and on the right shoulder, *GAṂ SARVĀKARṢIṆĪŚAKTYAI NAMAḤ*.

On the right side: *Ghaṃ* to the Śakti Sarvāhlādinī. On the right thigh: *Ṅaṃ* to the Śakti Sarvasaṃmohinī. On the right shank: *Caṃ* to the Śakti Sarvastambhinī. On the left shank: *Chaṃ* to the Śakti Sarvajambhinī. On the left thigh: *Jaṃ*.

To the Śakti who brings all under control, on the left side: *jhaṃ* to the Śakti who gladdens all; on the far end of the left: *ñaṃ* to the Śakti who causes universal intoxication; on the left cheek: *ṭaṃ* to the Śakti who accomplishes all aims; on the left side of the forehead: *ṭhaṃ* to the Śakti who fulfills all prosperity.

To Śakti (0), on the forehead (4): *ḍaṃ* to the Śakti consisting of all mantras (0). Below the crest-lock (4): *ḍhaṃ* salutation to the Śakti who causes the destruction of all dualities. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), [one places]: in the heart (4): *haiṃ ha klīṃ hasauḥ*, salutation to Tripuravāsinī, the Mistress of the Cakra. To her right (4): salutation to Īśitvaśrī.

On her left: *blūṃ sarvavaśyamudrāyai namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) as follows: "These are the Saṃpradāya-yoginīs, together with their mudrās, in the wheel that bestows all good fortune," and so forth. *Blūṃ*.
One should display the mudrā of universal subjugation (*sarvavaśyamudrā*). Thus ends the placement (*nyāsa*) of the fourth enclosure.

Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with: "Hrasaiṃ hrasklīṃ hrasauḥ, obeisance to the wheel that accomplishes all aims (*sarvārthasādhaka-cakra*)," and then, having performed the pervasive placement with: "Obeisance to the outer ten-spoked wheel (*bahirdaśāracakra*"), [one places it] in the right eye.

(4) *Namaḥ* to the Goddess who bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradādevī*). At the base of the nose: (4) *Taṃ* to the Goddess who bestows all prosperity (*sarvasaṃpatpradādevī*). In the left eye: (4) *Thaṃ* to the Goddess who makes everything dear (*sarvapriyaṃkarīdevī*). Above the left side of the belly: (4) *Daṃ* to the Goddess who brings about all auspiciousness (*sarvamaṅgalakāriṇīdevī*). Below the left side of the belly: (4)

*Dhaṃ* to the Goddess Sarvakāmapradādevī at the left knee; *naṃ* to the Goddess Sarvaduḥkhavimocinīdevī at the right knee; *paṃ* to the Goddess Sarvamṛtyupraśamanīdevī at the anus; *phaṃ* to the Goddess Sarvavighnavināśinīdevī below the right hip; *baṃ* to the Goddess Sarvāṅgasundarīdevī [at the same location].
Above the right side of the belly: (4) *Bhaṃ* salutation to the Goddess Sarvasaubhāgyadāyinī. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), at the heart:
(4) *Hasaiṃ Hsklīṃ Hasauḥ*, salutation to Tripurā, the Sovereign of the Śrīcakra. To her right: (4) *Vaśitva-śidhyai* salutation. To her left: (4) *Saḥ*, salutation to the Sarvonmādinī Mudrā. Thus.

Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*): "These Yoginīs of the Kulakaula, together with their mudrās, are in the wheel that accomplishes all aims," and so forth—one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). He [the practitioner] bestows the *Sarvonmādinī* mudrā.
Thus ends the placement of the fifth enclosure (*pañcamāvaraṇanyāsa*).
Then: *Hrīṃ klīṃ ble sarvarakṣākara cakrāya namaḥ*. Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with: *Tato 'ntardaśāracakrāya namaḥ*.

In the right nostril: *maṃ* to the goddess Sarvajñādevī, homage! In the right corner of the mouth: *yaṃ* to the goddess Sarvaśaktidevī. In the right breast: *raṃ* to the goddess Sarvaiśvaryapradādevī. In the right scrotum: *laṃ* to the goddess Sarvajñānamayīdevī. In the perineal suture: *vaṃ* to the goddess Sarvavyādhivināśinīdevī.

On the left scrotum (4): *śaṃ* to the Goddess whose nature is the support of all. On the left breast (4): *ṣaṃ* to the Goddess who removes all sins. On the left corner of the mouth (4): *saṃ* to the Goddess who consists of universal bliss. In the left nostril (4): *haṃ* to the Goddess whose nature is universal protection. At the tip of the nose (4): *kṣaṃ*.

Having performed the placement [of mantras] with: "Salutation to the Goddess who bestows all fruits while abiding everywhere"; then at the heart: (4) *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ*, "Salutation to Tripurāmālinī, the Sovereign of the Cakra. To her right: (4) "Salutation to the Siddhi of Prākāmya" (the power of irresistible will).
To her left: *kroṃ*, "Salutation to the Mahāṅkuśā Mudrā. Having performed the placement thus, these [mantras]:

One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) beginning with "The Nigarbha Yoginīs are present in the Cakra that bestows all protection," and so forth. One should display the hook-mudrā (aṅkuśa-mudrā) with the syllable *kroṃ*. This is the placement of the sixth enclosure (ṣaṣṭhāvaraṇanyāsa).

Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with: "(4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ* obeisance to the wheel that removes all diseases (*sarvarogahara-cakra*); then, obeisance to the eight-spoked wheel (*aṣṭāra-cakra*)," [one places the mantras as follows]: on the right side of the chin, "(4) *aṃ āṃ* (14) *blūṃ*, obeisance to Vaśinī, the Goddess of Speech (*vāgdevatā*); on the right part of the throat, "(4) *kaṃ* (4) *blūṃ hrīṃ*, [obeisance to] Kāmeśvarī."

To the Goddess of Speech (0): at the heart, on the right side (4), *aṃ āṃ* (14) *blūṃ*, obeisance to Vaśinī, the Goddess of Speech. At the navel, on the right side (4), *ṭaṃ* (4) *ylūṃ*, obeisance to Vimalā, the Goddess of Speech. At the navel, on the left side (4), *taṃ* (4) *jmrīṃ*, obeisance to Aruṇā, the Goddess of Speech.
Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*) as follows: on the left side of the heart, (4) *paṃ* (4) *hasalavyūṃ*, salutation to the goddess of speech Jayinī;

on the left side of the throat, (4) *yaṃ* (3) *jhamarayīṃ*, salutation to the goddess of speech Sarveśvarī; on the left side of the chin, (4) *śaṃkṣmrīṃ*, salutation to the goddess of speech Kaulinī. Then, at the heart, (4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ*.
*Sauḥ* to Tripurā Siddhā, the Mistress of the Cakra (*cakreśvarī*). To her right: *Bhukti-sidhyai*. To her left:

*Hasakhphraṃ*, salutation to Khecarīmudrā. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive ritual (*vyāpaka*) with the mantra: "These secret Yoginīs, together with their mudrās, [reside] in the cakra that removes all diseases," and so forth.
Reciting "hasakhphreṃ," one should display the khecarī mudrā; this is the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the seventh enclosure.
Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with "Obeisance to the Inner Wheel" (*antarālacakrāya namaḥ*), [one places] at the exterior of the heart-triangle,
on the right, left, left-right, and right-left [corners] (4): *drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ | yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ sāṃ | Obeisance to the Jambhanas, to Kāmeśvara, to Kāmeśvarī, and to the arrows.*

In the south-eastern part of the heart: *dhaṃ thaṃ* to the two enchantments (*mohanau*), to Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, and to the two bows, *namaḥ*. In the north-eastern part of the heart: *ā hrīṃ* to the two subjugations (*vaśīkaraṇau*), to Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, and to the two nooses, *namaḥ*. In the south-western part of the heart: *kroṃ kroṃ*.

"Obeisance to Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī with the *staṃbhana* [mudrās] and the *kuśas*; [obeisance] to the Heart in the northwest. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with: "(4) *hasraiṃ haslīṃ hasrauḥ*, obeisance to the Wheel that bestows all accomplishments; (4) obeisance to the Triangle Wheel. Then, at the front corner of the triangle: (4)

Having uttered the first peak-syllable (*prathakūṭa*), [one offers] obeisance to the goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī— the self-power of Rudra, whose essence is the power of will (*icchāśakti*), who resides in the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*) at the seat of Kāmagiri, who is the nature of Mitrīśanātha, and who is the presiding authority over the ten [powers].

In the left corner of the triangle (4), having uttered the second peak-syllable (*kūṭa*), [one offers] obeisance to the goddess Śrī Vajreśvarī, who is of the nature of the power of knowledge (*jñānaśakti*), whose essence is Viṣṇu, who resides in the solar wheel (*sūryacakra*) at the sacred seat of Jālandhara, who is the self-nature of Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha, and who presides over the state of dreaming (*svapnadaśā*).

In the south-eastern corner (4), having uttered the third peak-syllable, [one should say]: "Salutation to the goddess Śrī Bhagamālinī, who is the power of Brahman consisting of the energy of action (kriyā-śakti), who is of the nature of Uḍḍīśanātha in the Pīṭha of Pūrṇagiri within the lunar wheel (soma-cakra), and who presides over the state of deep sleep (suṣupti-daśā). Having thus performed the placement (vinyāsa), [one should place] *hasraiṃ* in the heart (4).

*Hasakalarīṃ hasrauḥ*, salutation to Tripurāmbikā, the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*). To her right: *(4)* salutation to Icchā-siddhi. To her left: *(4)* *hasauṃ*, salutation to the Sarvabīja-mudrā. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive application (*vyāpaka*) with the mantra: "These Yoginīs of the Parāpara-Rahasya, together with their mudrās, bestow all accomplishments in the wheel," and so forth.
One should perform [the rite] and display the seed-syllable mudrā (bījamudrā) with the syllable "hasauṃ"; this is the placement of the eight enclosures (aṣṭāvaraṇanyāsa).

Then, having uttered the fourth *vidyā*: "Salutation to the wheel consisting of all-bliss (*sarvānandamaya-cakra*); salutation to the *bindu*-wheel. Having thus performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*), one should utter the fourth *vidyā* in the center of the *bindu* within the heart-triangle, [saying]:
"In the Brahma-wheel (*brahmacakra*), at the great seat of Uḍḍiyāṇa (*mahoḍyāṇapīṭha*), [residing] in the nature of the venerable Caryānātha."
Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the Supreme Brahman-Self-Energy, who presides over the states of Turya and that which transcends Turya.
Having recited the Mūla-pancadaśī mantra right here in the heart, [salutation] to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the Sovereign of the Cakra.

Salutation! To her right: salutation to Prāptisiddhi. To her left: *Aiṃ*, salutation to Yonimudrā. Having thus performed the ritual placement (*vinyāsa*), she is the supreme and non-supreme secret Yoginī, the power of supreme nectar (*parāmṛtaśakti*), the mistress of all mantras, whose nature is the Supreme Brahman, residing in the Great Wheel (*mahācakra*) consisting of universal bliss.

O Sovereign of all vidyās, Sovereign of all pīṭhas, Sovereign of all vīras, Sovereign of all yogas, Sovereign of all speech, Sovereign of all siddhis; O Mother of the origin of the entire universe, together with your cakra, your deity, your mudrā, your siddhi, your weapon, your seat, your vehicle, your retinue, and your ornaments— [I worship you] with all ritual offerings.

"May the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, worshipped with the supreme (parā), the inferior (aparā), and the intermediate (parāparā) adoration, be well-pleased; salutations! Having thus performed the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-vinyāsa), once again, reciting the root mantra at the heart itself: "To the Sovereign of all the wheels (samastacakreśvarī), the venerable Mahātripurasundarī..."
Salutation to the Goddess. To her right: salutation to Sarvakāmasiddhi. To her left: *hasraiṃ hasakalmī hasrauḥ*, salutation to the Trikhaṇḍā Mudrā.
Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the heart itself, one should display the Yoni-mudrā. [The placement] is upon the heart-triangle, starting from the front.

Having performed the placement of the sixteen Nityās by means of their respective Nityā-vidyās— beginning with Ārā and ending with the fourth [Nityā], rotating counter-clockwise— one should visualize three lines on the rear portion of the heart-triangle,
and thereupon [place] the three rows of Gurus as will be described in the section on worship.

One should perform the placement (*nyāsa*). Then, in the intervals between the heart-triangle and the eight-cornered figure, one should place the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) and the young maidens (*yuvati*) according to the method to be described in the section on worship.

Having placed the five groups of five deities (*pañcapañcakadevatā*) within the center of the *binducakra* according to the method to be described, [one should proceed] to the back of the right shoulder...

Having placed the deities of the six locations— on the back of the ears, the temples, the forehead, the right nostril, the chin, and extending to the heart— and having placed the deities of the four commitments (*catuḥsamaya*) upon the *binducakra* itself in the manner to be described, one should then place [the deity] pervading all limbs with the fourth *vidyā*. Then...
Having recited the root mantra: O Goddess residing in the seat of Mahoḍyāna, Sovereign of all cakras, meditated upon;

seated upon a throne adorned with the five Śrīs, the five sheaths, the five Kalpalatās, the five wish-fulfilling cows, and the multitude of the five jewels; worshipped by all philosophical systems; praised by the youthful maidens of the six limbs.

Salutation to the Śrīpādukā of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī—the Goddess worshipped in the fourfold samaya; the generator of great good fortune; the bestower of great liberation; devoid of both emptiness and non-emptiness; endowed with power (Śakti); the Supreme Brahman who is Being-Consciousness-Bliss.

Thus, one should perform the threefold pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) from the crown of the head down to the feet. Then, having placed the sandals of one’s own Guru in the *brahmarandhra*, and having placed one’s own name—given by one’s Guru—at the *mūlādhāra*, one should meditate there upon the Great Kāmakalā. This is the Saṃhāra Śrīcakra Nyāsa.
Now begins the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Śrīcakra according to the order of emanation (sṛṣṭi).
There, having visualized a triangle on the head, one should utter the *turīyavidyā*: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*. Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*), one says:
"Obeisance to the Great Cakra consisting of all bliss; obeisance to the Bindu-cakra. Thus, one should perform the pervasive placement.

There, having uttered the fourth vidyā at the great bindu situated in the triangle of the head, and having performed the placement (nyāsa) as before— starting with "in the Brahma-cakra, at the venerable Mahoḍyāṇa-pīṭha," and so forth— one should utter the root-vidyā in the middle of the eyebrows and,
as previously, place that very same Cakreśvarī there; then, on her right and left sides, [one should perform] the attainment.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) as before for *siddhi*, *sarvakāmasiddhi*, the *yonimudrā*, and the *trikhaṇḍāmudrā*—[reciting] "This [is] the supreme-non-supreme secret; [I place] the Yoginīs in the Great Wheel consisting of universal bliss," and so forth as before—one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpakanyāsa*). [Reciting] "Aiṃ, the *yonimudrā*, Daḥ"—this is the placement of the *binducakra*.

Then, having visualized three lines on the rear portion of the triangle of the head, one should install there the three rows of Gurus from the section on worship to be described hereafter, preceded by the *praṇava*, the three *tārās*, and the dative case ending with *namaḥ*. Then,
at the locations for the placement of the sixteen vowels of the *mātṛkā*, [one should place] the *praṇava*, the three *tārās*, and so forth, followed by the dative case ending and *namaḥ*.

Having performed the placement of the sixteen Nityās with their respective names at the end [of each mantra] and by means of those respective Nityā-vidyās: (4) *hasraiṃ hasakalarīṃ hasrauḥ*, "Salutation to the wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradacakra*); salutation to the inner wheel (*antarālacakra*). Thus, [perform] the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*).
Having performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should place the previously mentioned weapon-deities with the understanding that they reside in the space between the triangle and the octagon.

It is as follows: in the right eye, (4) *drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ jaṃbhanebhyaḥ kāmeśvara-bāṇebhyo namaḥ* (Salutation to the piercing [arrows] of Kāmeśvara, *drāṃ drīṃ klīṃ blūṃ saḥ*, for the sake of crushing). In the left eye, *yāṃ rāṃ lāṃ vāṃ sāṃ*.

To the *jaṃbhanas*, Kāmeśvarī; to the arrows, obeisance. On the right eyebrow: *dhaṃ*, to the Enchanter, obeisance to the bow of Kāmeśvara. On the left eyebrow: *thaṃ*, to the Enchanter, obeisance to the bow of Kāmeśvarī. On the right ear: *āṃ*, to the Subjugator, obeisance to the noose of Kāmeśvara.
In the left ear: (4) Hrīṃ, obeisance to Kāmeśvarī, the noose for subjugation.
On the right nostril: *Kroṃ*, obeisance to the weapon-deity Kāmeśvara Kuśa for the purpose of paralyzing (*staṃbhana*).
On the left nostril: *Kroṃ*, obeisance to the weapon-deity Kāmeśvarī Kuśa for the purpose of paralyzing.
Having thus assigned the weapon-deities, one should [assign] the previously mentioned goddesses, Kāmeśvarī and the others, to the three corners of the triangle.

Having arranged the triad as before, one should place Tripurāmbikā, the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*), in the heart as before. Having placed Icchāsiddhi and the Seed-Syllable Gesture (*bījamudrā*) upon her chest and left side, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with the words: "These are the Parāpararahasya Yoginīs, together with their gestures, in the wheel that bestows all accomplishments," and so forth. Then: *hrīṃ*.

*Śrīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to the wheel that removes all diseases; obeisance to the eight-spoked wheel. Having thus performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*), one should, beginning from the front part of the head, sequentially [place] the previously mentioned *muṇḍamālā* (garland of skulls) upon the eight locations.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the eight deities of speech, beginning with Vaśinī, [one should place] Tripurā Siddhā—the previously mentioned mistress of the wheel (*cakreśvarī*)—upon the Maṇipūraka cakra. Then, having placed the accomplishment of enjoyment (*bhukti-siddhi*) on its right and left [spokes], and the Khecarī mudrā as well;
[these are] the secret Yoginīs in the wheel that removes all diseases, together with their mudrās, and so forth.
One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*).

(2) Then, (4) having performed the pervasive placement with the mantra: *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ sarvarakṣākara cakrāya namaḥ*, [one places it] on the right eye, its root, its outer corner, the right ear, its back, the crest, and the crown of the head.

Having placed the ten Śaktis, beginning with Sarvajñā as previously described, in the ten locations— the right side, the left side, the back of the left ear, the left ear, the left corner of the eye, the root of the left eye, and the two breasts— and having placed Tripuramālinī, the previously mentioned Mistress of the Wheel (cakreśvarī), in the Svādhiṣṭhāna wheel, [one should place her] on its axis...

Having stepped forward with the two left [hands], having placed the *mudrā* of the Great Hook (*mahāṅkuśā*) for the accomplishment as before, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) starting with:
"These are the womb-yoginīs in the wheel that performs all protection, together with their *mudrās*," and so forth.
Then, having performed the pervasive placement with *hasaiṃ hasklīṃ hasauḥ*, [one places them] at the throat in the Viśuddhi [cakra].

On the sixteen petals of the wheel, one should place one Śakti on each petal; in this sequence, having placed the powers up to the seventh Śakti, one should place the remaining three Śaktis on the three leftover petals. Thus, by proceeding clockwise, one should place the ten Śaktis beginning with Sarvasiddhipradā.

Having installed Tripurācakreśvarī at the Mūlādhāra as before, and having installed the *vaśitva* siddhi and the Unmādinī mudrā on its left and right sides respectively as before, one should perform the pervasive installation (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) beginning with: "These Kulakaula Yoginīs, together with their mudrās, reside in the Sarvārthasādhaka-cakra," and so forth. HAIṂ HAKLĪṂ HASAUḤ.

"Obeisance to the Cakra that bestows all good fortune. Having thus performed the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-vinyāsa), one should place the ten Śaktis beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇī upon the ten petals of the twelve-petaled Anāhata lotus at the heart; then, on each of the final two petals, one should place two Śaktis each.

"One should place the four remaining powers"—having thus placed the fourteen powers; having placed Tripuravāsinī, the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*), as previously described upon the two *ūt* syllables; and having placed the attainment of mastery (*īśitvasiddhi*) and the *vaśya*-mudrā on her right and left sides as before—these are the *yoginīs* of the oral tradition (*saṃpradāya*).

One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the mantra beginning "O bestower of all good fortune, [residing] in the wheel," and so forth. (4) Then, having performed the pervasive placement with "Hrīṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to the wheel that agitates all (*sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra*"),
one should place [the mantras] on the spinal column, the left side, the middle of the abdomen, the right side of the abdomen, and the middle [of the back].

Having placed the four Śaktis previously mentioned, beginning with Anaṅgakusumā, in the four locations between the right side and the backbone, one should then place them in the following places: between the backbone and the left side, between the left side and the abdomen,
between the abdomen and the right side, and [between] the right side...
Having placed the four powers, beginning with Anaṅgarekhā, in the four locations between the two spinal columns;

and having placed Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Cakra, as previously described upon both knees, and having placed Mahimāsiddhi and the Ākarṣaṇī Mudrā on her right and left sides—these [should be worshipped]. (4)
One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the mantra: "The most secret Yoginīs, together with their mudrās, in the wheel that agitates all," and so forth.

(9) Then, having performed the pervasive placement with: "Aiṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ, obeisance to the wheel that fulfills all desires" (4), one should place [the mantras] in the six-petaled lotus of the *svādhiṣṭhāna*, starting from the eastern petal and proceeding clockwise through five of the petals.
Having placed the three powers on each petal and a single power on the final petal—

thus assigning the sixteen powers beginning with Kāmākarṣiṇī— one should assign Tripureśvarī, as previously mentioned, to the two shanks; and Laghimāsiddhi and Drāviṇīmudrā to her right and left [sides].

Having placed these Guptayoginīs, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) with the mantra beginning "to the wheel that fulfills all desires, together with the mudrās," and so forth. (8) Then, (4) having performed the pervasive placement with "Aṃ Āṃ Sauḥ, to the Trailokyamohanacakra," and having performed the pervasive placement with "Salutation to the inner square line," [one should place them] at the *mūlādhāra*.

One should place the ten previously mentioned mudrās, beginning with Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇī, upon the four petals of the four-petaled lotus and within its four intermediate spaces— specifically, between the eastern petal and the northeast intermediate space, between the western petal and the southwest intermediate space, and so forth.

Then, having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with "Salutation to the central line of the outer square," one should place the eight previously mentioned powers, Brāhmī and the others, in order on the right shank at the cardinal and intermediate directions. Then, having performed the pervasive placement with "Salutation to the outer line of the square," [one should place them] on the left shank at the cardinal and intermediate directions.

Having sequentially assigned the eight previously mentioned supernatural powers (*siddhis*), beginning with *aṇimā*, one should assign the power of *prāpti* to the right foot and the power of *sarvakāma* to the left foot. Then, having assigned Tripurā, the Mistress of the Wheel (*cakreśvarī*), to both feet as before, one should assign the power of *aṇimā* and [the mudrā] Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī to her right and left [sides].

Having applied the mudrās and performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-vinyāsa*) with the words, "These manifest Yoginīs, together with their mudrās, [reside] in the wheel that deludes the three worlds," and so forth, one should meditate upon oneself as non-different from the radiant Śrī Mahātripurasundarī. Thus concludes the emanation-placement (*sṛṣṭi-nyāsa*) of the Śrīcakra.
Now follows the placement of the Śrīcakra (sthiti-śrīcakranyāsa).

And that [practice] consists of three parts: the Vidyā, the Cakra, and the Cakreśvarī. Therein, first, according to the tradition, one should perform the purification of the hands (*karaśuddhi*) with the Vidyā as before—namely, *aṃ āṃ sauḥ*—and having performed that and likewise deposited it [on the body], one should likewise effect self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*) with *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, and then begin the ritual deposition (*nyāsa*). Therein, at the outset:

The threefold placement of the Root-Vidyā (*mūlavidyānyāsa*) is as follows: On the head: *namaḥ* to the first *kūṭa*. In the secret place: *namaḥ* to the second *kūṭa*. In the heart: *namaḥ* to the third *kūṭa*. In the right eye: *pra* [to the first *kūṭa*]. In the left eye: *dvitīya* [to the second *kūṭa*]. On the forehead: *tṛtīya* [to the third *kūṭa*]. In the right ear: *pra* [to the first *kūṭa*].
At the left ear: *dvi-kū*. At the mouth: *tri-kū*. At the right shoulder: *pra-kū*. At the left shoulder:
*dvi-kū*. At the back: *tṛtīya-kū*. At the right knee: *pra-kū*. At the left knee: *dvitīya-kū*.
*Kū* at the navel; *tṛ* *kū* *namaḥ*. Thus is the deposition of the *kūṭas* of the root-vidyā. *Kaṃ namaḥ* on the head; *eṃ namaḥ* in the secret place; *īṃ* in the heart; *laṃ* in the right eye;
*hrīṃ namaḥ* in the left eye; *haṃ namaḥ* in the forehead eye; *saṃ namaḥ* in the right ear; [and] *vaṃ namaḥ* in the left ear.

Kaṃ namaḥ on the face; (4) Haṃ namaḥ on the right arm; (4) Laṃ namaḥ on the left arm; (4) Hrīṃ namaḥ on the back; (4) Saṃ namaḥ on the right knee; (4) Kaṃ namaḥ on the left knee; (4) Laṃ namaḥ at the navel; (4) Hrīṃ namaḥ at the navel. This is the placement of the syllables (*akṣaranyāsa*). [Then recite] the entire root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*).

One should perform the threefold placement (*nyāsa*) as follows: [first] the fifteen-syllable mantra beginning with *praṇava* and *tārā* and ending with *namaḥ*, placing it individually upon each of the previously mentioned fifteen locations from the crown of the head down to the navel. [Second] the four-syllable mantra: *aṃ āṃ sauḥ namaḥ* on the two feet;
*aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ* on the two shanks; *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ namaḥ* on the two knees; *haiṃ hasklīṃ* on the two thighs.

*Hasauḥ* *namaḥ*. At the tip of the *liṅga* (4): *hasaiṃ hasklīṃ hasauḥ namaḥ*. At the *mūlādhāra* (4): *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the Mūrtividyā, [one recites]:
(2) *haṃ klī* (2). Or, at the *anāhata* [cakra], one recites *hasraiṃ hasklīṃ hasrauḥ namaḥ*; this is the Āvāhanī Vidyā.
Vinyāsa: (4) *hasakalaraḍaiṃ*, *hasakalaraḍīṃ*, *hasakalaraḍauḥ*—salutation to the Brahma-randhra.
Then, [one should perform the placement] of the root-mantra from the head to the feet, and from the feet to the heart.

One should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*). Then, at the *mūlādhāra*: (4) *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ |* "Salutation to the wheel that fulfills all desires (*sarvāśāparipūraka-cakra*). At the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: (4) *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ |* "Salutation to the wheel that agitates all (*sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra*). At the *maṇipūraka*: (4) (4) *hai haklīṃ hasauḥ |*

Salutation to the Cakra that bestows all good fortune. In the Anāhata [cakra]: (4) *hasaiṃ hasklīṃ hasauḥ*, salutation to the Cakra that accomplishes all aims. In the Viśuddhi-cakra: (4) *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ*, salutation to the Cakra of the protection of all. At the tip of the uvula (*laṃbikā*): (4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ*.

Salutation to the Cakra that removes all diseases. At the Ājñā [cakra]: (4) *hasraiṃ hasklīṃ hasrauḥ*, salutation to the Cakra that bestows all accomplishments. In the Bindu: (4) having uttered the fifteen-syllable root mantra (*mūlamantra*), salutation to the Śrī Mahācakra consisting of all bliss. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) of the nine cakras.
One should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Mistress of the Nine Wheels.

Therein, first, in the Trailokyamohana-cakra placed below the Mūlādhāra: (4) *aṃ āṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to Tripurācakreśvarī. In the Sarvāśāparipūraka-cakra situated at the Mūlādhāra: (4) *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to Tripureśvarīcakreśvarī. [In the] Svādhiṣṭhāna-situated...

In the *Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa* cakra (4): *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*. Homage to Tripurasundarī, the Mistress of the Cakra (*cakreśvarī*). In the *Sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka* cakra situated in the *maṇipūra* (4): *hai haklīṃ hasauḥ*. Homage to Tripuravāsinī, the Mistress of the Cakra. In the *Sarvārthasādhaka* cakra situated in the *anāhata* (4): *hasauṃ hasklīṃ*.
Hasauḥ, salutation to Tripurā Śrīcakreśvarī. In the Viśuddhi-cakra, which bestows all protection, (4) Hrīṃ Klīṃ Bleṃ, salutation to Tripuramālinī Cakreśvarī.

To the Goddess Tripurāsiddhā, the Mistress of the Wheel, who resides at the tip of the *laṃbikā* (the uvula) in the wheel that removes all diseases: *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ tripurā siddhā cakreśvaryai namaḥ*. To the Goddess Tripurāmbikā, the Mistress of the Wheel, who resides in the *ājñā-cakra* in the wheel that bestows all perfections (*siddhis*): *hasraiṃ hasakalarīṃ hasrauḥ tripurāṃbikā cakreśvaryai namaḥ*. [She] who resides in the Great Bindu...

Having uttered the root fifteen-syllable mantra at the *binducakra* (4), [one should say]: "Obeisance to the *śrīpādukā* of Mahātripurasundarī, the Great Mistress of the Wheel. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*) and having clearly meditated upon each respective wheel as being joined with one another and presided over by their respective mistresses, once again—

Having performed the purification of the hands (*karaśuddhi*), having performed self-protection (*ātmarakṣā*) by means of Tripurasundarī, and having applied the previously mentioned six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*): one should apply the *vāgbhava* syllable at the *mūlādhāra*, the *kāmarāja* at the heart, the third [syllable] between the eyebrows, and the fourth *vidyā* at the *brahmarandhra*. Then, [one should apply] the entire [mantra], both manifest, secret, and most secret...

"Salutation to the Śrīcakra, to the Yoginīs, and to the Śrīpādukās of the Saṃpradāya, Kulakaula, Nigarbha, Rahasya, Parāpara-Rahasya, and Parāparātira-hasya. Thus, meditating upon one's own body as having the form of the Śrīcakra, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). This is the Śrī-sthiti-Śrīcakranyāsa.
Now, the fruit of the Śrīcakra-nyāsa.
In that regard, it is stated in the Rudrayāmala:
The practitioner who, with a steady mind, performs this placement within the body in this manner, shall immediately abandon the human state and attain the nature of Śiva. (1)
Whoever wears it at the three times of day, it shall be joined to all his limbs.
O Goddess, the entire state of the Yoginī shines forth perpetually. (2)
The earth becomes a field for twelve yojanas.
Thus has this Nyāsa been told to you, O blessed lady, which is difficult to obtain even in the three worlds. (3)
One should reveal it to a disciple who is endowed with devotion, or to a practitioner;
one should not show it to practitioners who have fallen from their path, nor to mere kinsmen. (4)
"If it is given, there will be a loss of accomplishment"—this is considered the command of Śaṅkara.
The mantras turn away from her, and the beautiful woman becomes angry. (5)
And it would become impure for him; therefore, he should guard it with effort.
Thus ends the threefold Śrīcakra-nyāsa.
By Śrīvidyānandanātha, the beloved son of Śiva and Umā.
Thus, the seventh wave in the Ocean of the Jewels of Good Fortune has come to an end. (1)
[Thus ends the seventh wave in the *Saubhāgyaratnākara*, composed by Śrī Śrīvidyānandanātha, who dwells at the pair of lotus feet of the venerable Saccidānandanātha. (7)
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) beginning with the purification of the hands (karaśuddhi).

Therein, first, one should perform the placement of the seat (*āsana-nyāsa*) by placing, according to the previously mentioned sequence of the hands from the middle fingers to the palms, the mantra of the first *Cakreśvarī* as stated before. That [placement] is of two kinds:
the four-seat placement (*caturāsana-nyāsa*) and the six-seat placement (*ṣaḍāsana-nyāsa*). Of these, first is the four-seat placement.
For example: at the two feet—(4) *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, salutation to the seat of the self of the goddess Tripurasundarī.
At the two shanks—(4) *haiṃ haklīṃ hasauḥ*, salutation to the seat of all wheels (*cakras*) of Tripurāvāsinī.
At the two knees: (4) *hasaiṃ hasakalīṃ hasauḥ*, obeisance to Tripurā, the seat of all mantras (*sarvamantrāsanāya namaḥ*).
In the *mūlādhāra*: *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ*, [salutation] to Tripuramālinī, the seat of the accomplished goal (*sādhyasiddhāsana*).
Thus is the ritual placement of the four seats (*caturāsananyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement of the six seats (ṣaḍāsananyāsa).

There, at the two feet: (4) *aṃ āṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to Tripurāsudhārṇava, whose seat is the ocean of nectar. At the two knees: (4) *eṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to Tripureśvarī, whose seat is the lotus of light. At the two thighs: (4) *hrīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, obeisance to the Goddess Tripurasundarī, whose seat is the Self. At the two buttocks: (4) *haiṃ haklīṃ hasauḥ*.

*Tripuravāsinī*, salutation to the seat of all *cakras*. At the anus: (4) *hasaiṃ hasklīṃ hasauḥ*, salutation to *Tripurā Śrī*, the seat of all mantras. At the *mūlādhāra*: (4) *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ*, salutation to *Tripuramālinī*, the seat of the accomplished and the to-be-accomplished. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six seats.
Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).

And that [protection] is threefold: the six-limbed placement for protection (*rakṣā-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*), the six-limbed placement of the root-mantra (*mūla-vidyā-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*), and the six-limbed placement of the young maidens (*ṣaḍaṅga-yuvatī-nyāsa*). Among these, first is the six-limbed placement for protection. It is as follows: (4) *Eṃ Klīṃ Sauḥ!
Obeisance to Tripurasundarī! Protect me, protect me! Obeisance to the heart.* In this same manner, [it is applied] to the six limbs.
One should perform the placement (nyāsa) together with the respective mudrās and the respective mantras.
Now follows the root six-limbed placement (mūla-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa).
This is to be understood as the placement at the locations of the six limbs, performed by repeating the three root syllables twice, as previously described.

The worshipers of the sixteen-syllable mantra should perform the root six-limbed placement (*mūla-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa*) as follows: the heart is formed by the first five seed-syllables; the head by the three seed-syllables following that;

the three limbs from the crest-lock (*śikhā*) to the eyes by the three peak-syllables (*kūṭa*) situated above those; and the weapon (*astra*) by the final five seed-syllables. Thus the root six-limbed placement is to be performed.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six-limbed maiden.
And that [mantra] is of two kinds, due to the distinction between the yoga of Bālā and Mūlavidyā. First, there is the placement (nyāsa) of the yoga of Bālā:
therein, (4) *eṃ* to the heart of the All-Knowing One, *namaḥ*; (4) *klīṃ* to the head of the Ever-Satisfied One, *svāhā*;
(4) *sauḥ* to the crest-lock of the Beginningless Awakened One, *vaṣaṭ*; (4) *eṃ* to the armor of the Self-Independent One, *huṃ*; (4) *klīṃ*.
Vauṣaṭ ṣaṭ to the three eyes that are eternally undiminished. Sauḥ Aṃ, Phaṭ to the weapon for Anantā.
Now follows the placement of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅga*) of the Youthful Goddess (*yuvatīnyāsa*).

Therein: (4) The first *kūṭa*: O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, obeisance to the Heart, the abode of the power of omniscience (*sarvajñatā-śakti*). (4) The second *kūṭa*: O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, *svāhā* to the Head, the abode of the power of eternal contentment (*nityatṛpti-śakti*). (4) The third *kūṭa*: O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, [the abode of] the power of beginninglessness (*anādi*...).
To the crest-lock [of the Goddess] who is the abode of the power of awakening, Vaṣaṭ! (4) Again, the first peak-syllable:

To Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the abode of the independent power, for the armor, Haṃ! (4) The second peak-syllable: To Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the abode of the eternally undiminished power, for the three eyes, Vauṣaṭ! (4)
The third peak: O Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, to the abode of infinite power, [homage] to the weapon, Phaṭ!
Thus concludes the six-limbed placement of the young woman (ṣaḍaṅga-yuvatī-nyāsa).
Now follows the sequential placement (nyāsa) according to the tradition of the Kāmakalā.

Therein, first, as before, having meditated upon the Guru’s sandals on one's own head, having worshipped and prostrated, [one places] the first *kūṭa* on the right shoulder: *haṃsaḥ prakāśacaraṇābhyāṃ namaḥ*.
On the left shoulder (4), the second peak: *so'haṃ*—salutation to the feet of *vimarśa*. In the heart (4), the third peak: *haṃsaḥ so'haṃ*—salutation to the feet of *prakāśa-vimarśa*.
Having recited the fourth Vidyā at the crown of the head— *Haṃsaḥ Śivaḥ So’haṃ Nirvāṇacaraṇābhyāṃ Namaḥ*— and having prostrated before the four feet with palms joined in reverence (*añjali*).

Of the Kāmakalāpāraṃparyanyāsa: (4) Kāmeśvara is the seer (ṛṣi); (4) Paṅkti is the meter (chandaḥ); (4) the supreme consciousness-aspect (kalā), Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, is the deity; (0) the application (viniyoga) is for the sake of attaining the grace of the venerable Supreme Deity. Having thus recollected the seer and so forth, one should perform the placement (nyāsa). (4)

Having performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the six limbs upon the hands using the syllable *ĀM* and the other six long vowels, and having performed the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) of the venerable Root Mantra in the form of the *Kāmakalā* enclosed by the *Praṇava*, one should perform the meditation (*dhyāna*).
It is as follows:
Standing in the midst of light, possessing a universal form, three-eyed, and bestowing the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness.
I worship her who has the hue of vermilion, whose limbs are exceedingly delicate, who consists of both illusion and ultimate reality. (1)

Having meditated thus, one should visualize the venerable fifteen-syllabled root mantra in its previously described form, extending from the base (mūlādhāra) to the aperture of Brahmā (brahmarandhra).

Through the dissolution of each individual syllable of that mantra, one should leave remaining only the final digit (kalā), which takes the form of the fourth vowel and resides in the aperture of Brahmā. Then, one should contemplate that very [digit] as containing within it the fifteen syllables.

One should meditate upon the *Kāmakalā*, which consists of the experience of one’s own self and is of the nature of *sac-cid-ānanda* (Being-Consciousness-Bliss), transformed into the form of the fourth vowel (*turya-svara*), and install it at the navel. There, at the navel, one should install [the mantra] with the thumb, index, middle, and ring fingers, saying: "*(4) Īṃ, salutation."* Then, on the left side of the navel, [one installs] "*(4) Sac-cid-ānanda..."*

*Paramasaṃvit īṃ namaḥ*. To the right of the navel: *Saccidānanda Paramasaṃvit īṃ namaḥ*. One should place these two [mantras] with the middle, ring, and thumb fingers. Then follows the placement of the four feet.
Therein, on the head, at the front corner of the triangle: *īṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, *haṃsaḥ*.
Salutation to the two feet of Light (*prakāśa*). In the left corner (4): the second *kūṭa*, *so'haṃ*;
salutation to the two feet of Reflection (*vimarśa*). In the right corner (4): the third *kūṭa*, *haṃsaḥ so'haṃ*;
salutation to the two feet of Light and Reflection (*prakāśavimarśa*). In the center (4): having uttered the fourth Vidyā, *haṃsaḥ*.

"I am that Śiva; salutations to the two feet of Nirvāṇa. Having thus assigned the four feet by means of the *saṃghaṭa-mudrā* held in the right and left hands—which consist of Śiva and Śakti—one should then worship on the rear line of the triangle: (4) "I worship the *śrīpādukā* of Sakalānandanātha; salutations. (4)
I worship the venerable sandals of Niṣkalānandanātha; salutations!

(4) I worship the venerable sandals of Navātmānandanātha; (4) I worship the venerable sandals of Akūrānandanātha. Thus, one worships the four Gurus in a linear sequence, beginning from one's own right.

Having placed [the mantra] at the end of the left [hand], [one should worship] in the center of the triangle of the head: (4) *Īṃ*, the digit of supreme consciousness (*paramasaṃvitkalā*), the venerable *Mahātripurasundarī*, the venerable *śrīpādukāṃ pū* [jayāmi]. In the circle of the face:
(4) *Īṃ*, obeisance to the curved one (*vakra*) above the point (*bindu*) of Nandanātha, who possesses the digit of the half of the supreme (*saparārddhakalā*).
On the two breasts (4): *īṃ* [with] the half-measure of the subsequent [syllable], obeisance to the two breasts below Nandanātha, which possess two *bindus*.

Having thus placed these two [fingers] with the thumb, middle finger, and ring finger, one should install [the mantra] at the place of the *yoni* with the *yonimudrā*: "Īṃ, to the *yoni* of the blissful lord of the digits (*kalā*) beyond the half-cycle of time (*parārdha*), which is manifested by the lines, salutation!
Thus one should install it with the *yonimudrā*.

Then, having performed the previously mentioned nyāsa of the ṛṣis, and having applied the six-limbed (ṣaḍaṅga) nyāsa first in reverse order— beginning with the ṛṣis and so forth— followed by the hand-nyāsa (karanyāsa), and finally the nyāsa of the ṛṣis and so forth;
and having meditated upon oneself as the form of the Goddess as previously described, [one should recite] the Vāmakalā-vidyā according to one's capacity.
"One should recite" refers to the transmission of the Kāmakalā lineage and its ritual placement (nyāsa).
Now follows the internal placement of Kāmakalā.

And that [speech] is fourfold, through the divisions of Parā, Paśyantī, Madhyamā, and Vaikharī. Among these, first is the placement (nyāsa) of Parā. It is as follows: having visualized a red, full moon-maṇḍala within the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus at the Brahma-randhra, which is below the face of Aruṇa.

In the center of that, having meditated upon a *śṛṅgāṭa* (triangular seat) resembling the rising sun, with its own crest at the root and tip, and having meditated within it upon the *vāgbhava* [syllable]— which consists of all letters in the sequence beginning with *a*, *ka*, and *tha*— as the seat of *Akula*; and in the middle of that, the collection of letters beginning with *ha*, *kṣa*, *pa*, and *śca*.
Having meditated upon the unsurpassed, blazing, colorless form whose nature is supreme bliss,
one should contemplate the Akula Kuṇḍalinī— whose form is the half-moon digit (ardhakalā), white like a lotus fiber— arising from the center of that [form] at the root-triangle (mūla-śṛṅgāṭaka).
Having meditated upon the Great Kāmakalā, the Amṛtakuṇḍalinī, which is uninterrupted up to the center,

one should likewise meditate upon the Śṛṅgāṭa (triangle) at the tip of the front corner of the triangle within the fire-maṇḍala at the pericarp of the four-petalled lotus in the Mūlādhāra, as previously described; and within that—
As before, having visualized the Vāgbhava seat of the Kula, one should contemplate within it the previously mentioned *manatka*.
From its center, the *agni-kuṇḍalinī*, the *kāmakalā* consisting of the digit (*kalā*) of the supreme limit (*parārdha*),
resembling a blazing fire, enters the central path, pierces the mass of knots, and [reaches] that *akula*.

Having meditated upon the *akula* [principle] as having reached above the feet, one should cause it to enter by means of the *liṅga* in the form of a staff-like flame situated in the center of the intellect; then, through the friction arising from the churning of those two— the *kuṇḍalinī* of nectar and the *liṅga* of fire,
which take the forms of the *yoni* and the *liṅga*— there arises a continuous and dense flow of red [nectar].

Having meditated upon oneself as being sprinkled and filled with the "dead-filling" (mṛtapūra), one should contemplate both as the Supreme Power (Parā-śakti) in the form of a single resonance (nāda) arising from their state of aesthetic identity (sāmarasya).
Thus ends the Parā-nyāsa. As for its definition, it is found in the Bhairavayāmala:
Situated within the intervals, situated in the midst of the intervals, and moving within that which is most deeply situated within the intervals.
The one who possesses all knowledge knows him who stands within the boat of *taraṃ*.
Indeed, it is devoid of head, hands, and feet; it is the imperishable, supreme, and the remover of the afflictions of existence.
He in whose heart's cavity [the Lord] dwells perfectly, by him even death has been reduced to ashes. (2)
The Śaiva and likewise the Śākta [forms], while the state of equilibrium (sāmarasya) is the intermediate one.
When it has become unified at that time, then its color is supreme. (3)
From emptiness, the expansion has arisen; from that expansion, the timeless [state] has emerged.
The reality that has arisen from the Unmanifest is the universe, which exists in fivefold form. (4)
He who is devoid of the states of meditative absorption and is free from the utterance of forms.
Unstruck, it resounds within; established in the state of the mouth-to-mouth union. (5)
Devoid of the three abodes and situated within the mouths of the Yogeshīs, he is truly released by them as they themselves speak the truth. (6)
Śambhu is void, from him arises Śakti, and from Śakti arises the abode consisting of the triad.
And from that, the entire collection of primordial phonemes shall arise. (7)
That very [practice] is said to be unsurpassed, granting the siddhis of the Kaula tradition immediately.
And in that same manner, it would be situated between the moon and the sun. (8)
The letter *ta* is the abode of Soma, while the first *repha* (*ra*) is the Sun;
the Fire moves like a staff, and that which consists of them is unified as one. Thus [it is said]. (9)
Now follows the placement (nyāsa) for Paśyantī.

Therein, having meditated upon the cluster of primordial phonemes filled with the essence of Brahman within the *brahmarandhra*— the *akula*-lotus mentioned previously— and having recollected the eleven-fold *paśyantī* form, which is filled with that same essence through its state of aesthetic fusion (*sāmarasya*), one should perform the ritual placement (*nyāsa*).

There, having visualized a triangle with its apex facing oneself upon the head, one should contemplate the triad and pentad by moving counter-clockwise from the tip of that [triangle], starting from the tip of the left line and ending at the tip of the right line.

Thus, one should sequentially assign the eleven *kalās* beginning with Vāmā. As follows: (4) *Namaḥ* to Vāmā; (4) *Namaḥ* to Jyeṣṭhā; (4) *Namaḥ* to Raudrī. Thus on the left line. (4) *Namaḥ* to Ambikā;
(4) *Namaḥ* to Icchā; (4) *Namaḥ* to Jñānā; (4) *Namaḥ* to Kriyā; (4) *Namaḥ* to Śāntā.
Thus on the rear line. (4) "Salutation to her whose essence is the letter *a*; salutation to her whose essence is the letter *ha*;
salutation to her whose essence is the flavor of *aha*. Thus one should place [these mantras] on the right line. This is the *paśyatī* placement (*nyāsa*).
Now follows the middle placement (*madhyamā nyāsa*).

And that [nāda] is of two kinds, distinguished as subtle and gross. Therein: (4) at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*), "Obeisance to the unmodified nāda, whose essence is the letter *a*. (4) At the forehead, "Obeisance to the nāda of emptiness, whose essence is the letter *a*."
In the *ājñācakra* (4): salutation to the grasping of touch, whose nature consists of two points (*bindu*), [to the letter] *Aṃ*. At the tip of the *laṃbikā* (4):

This is the subtle-middling (*sūkṣma-madhyama*) nyāsa.
Now follows the placement (nyāsa) of the gross and the intermediate [levels].

Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) for the time of death.

Having formed the *trikhaṇḍā-mudrā* with the five-peak mantra *hasraim ha klīṃ hasrauḥ* and performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*), one should meditate upon the phonemes whose radiance blazes from being sprinkled by the rain of the nectar of consciousness.
Then, having invoked [the deity] in the form of the *kāmakalā* within the six *ādhāras* with the mantra "internal fire that consumes darkness,"...
One should contemplate the Goddess within oneself.
Thus ends the internal placement of the Kāmakalās. Now follows the external placement of the Kāmakalās.

Therein, one should meditate upon the face of the Self— which is the primordial *bindu* of the fourth vowel (*turyasvara*) accompanied by the *bindu*, being the root of the *Kāmakalā*— as endowed with the limbs of hair, eyes, ears, nose, and so forth; and below that, having visualized the two *bindus* as the two breasts, endowed with the four arms and other limbs.

Having meditated upon his heart-portion (*hārddhakalā*) together with the two feet and other limbs as the *yoni*, one should utter the *vāgbhava* peak-syllable (*kūṭa*) and [offer salutation] to the two breasts of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, who consists of the bindu above the syllable *īṃ* and is endowed with the hair and other limbs, saying: "Salutation to the two breasts" (*stanadvayāya namaḥ*), and "Salutation to the face" (*vaktrāya namaḥ*). (4)

Having uttered the *kāmarāja-kūṭa*, [one offers salutation] to the two breasts, together with the four arms and other limbs, of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, who is the nature of the two *bindus* below the syllable *īṃ*: *namaḥ*.
(4) Having uttered the third *kūṭa*, [one offers salutation] to that which is the nature of the half-moon (*ardhakalā*) of the syllable *īṃ*.
"Salutation to the Yoni, together with the two feet and other limbs of Śrī Mahātripurasundarī.

(4) Thus, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) as a pervasive extension from the head to the throat, from the throat to the navel, and from the navel to the tips of the feet. (4) Having recited the Root Mantra (*mūlavidyā*), [one should place] the whole...
"Salutation to all the limbs of the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, whose essence is the Kāmakalā.
Having thus performed the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) over all the limbs.

Having meditated upon the nose, forehead, eyes, ears, and face as being within the bindu of the mouth; the four arms, chest, heart, and breasts as being within the bindu of the breasts; and the two feet as being within the bindu of the womb; one should then contemplate her as complete in all her limbs, consisting of the supreme syllable that has become the unified Kāmakalā.

One should meditate upon oneself as the Goddess, who possesses supreme beauty, who rests in the lap of Kāmeśvara, and who is adorned with all ornaments. Thus ends the external placement of the Kāmakalā.
Now follows the ritual placement of the weapons (āyudhanyāsa).

Triḥ (0) | (4) Phaṃ Vajreśvarī Triḥ (0) | (4) Baṃ Kṣobhiṇī Triḥ (0) | (4) Bhaṃ Śāmbhavī Triḥ (0) | (4) Maṃ Stambhinī Triḥ (0) | (4) Yaṃ Anāmā Triḥ (0) | (4) Raṃ Raktā Triḥ (0) | (4) Laṃ Śuklā Triḥ (0) | (4) Vaṃ Aparājitā Triḥ (0) | (4) Śaṃ Saṃvarttakā Triḥ (0) | (4) Ṣaṃ Vimalā Triḥ (0) | (4) Saṃ Ghorā Triḥ (0) | (4) Triḥ (0) ||
Haṃ Aghorā Triṃ; Laṃ Bindubhairavī Triṃ; Kṣaṃ Sarvākarṣaṇī Tripurāyai Namaḥ. These Mātṛkās are to be deposited in their respective locations. Thus ends the fifty-fold Nyāsa of Tripurā.
Now follows the sixteen-fold deposition of the Kāmakalās.

There, on the right foot: *klīṃ aṃ* salutation to Siddhākalā. On the right calf: *klīṃ āṃ* salutation to Prītikalā. On the right knee: *klīṃ iṃ* salutation to Ratikalā. On the right thigh: *klīṃ īṃ* salutation to Dhṛtikalā. On the right chest: *klīṃ uṃ* salutation to Kāntikalā. On the right armpit: *klīṃ ūṃ*... [salutation to Saumyākalā].

*klīṃ ūṃ* to the digit Manoramā on the right side of the face; *klīṃ ṛṃ* to the digit Manoharā on the right head; *klīṃ ṝṃ* to the digit Manobhavā on the left side of the head; *klīṃ ḷṃ* to the digit Madanonmādinī on the left side of the head.

On the left face: *klīṃ l̥ṃ* to the digit Mohinī. At the root of the left arm: *klīṃ e* to the digit Dīpinī. On the left chest: *klīṃ aiṃ* to the digit Śoṣiṇī. On the left thigh: *klīṃ oṃ* to the digit Vaśaṅkarī. On the left knee: *klīṃ auṃ* to the digit Rañjinī.

On the left calf: *klīṃ aṃ* to Subhagā Kalā; on the left foot: *klīṃ aḥ* to Priyadarśanī Kalā, *namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*nyāsa*), these [deities] are to be meditated upon as white in color, holding blue lotuses in their hands. This is the placement of the sixteen Kāmakalās.
Now follows the placement of the sixteen lunar digits (*somakalā*).

Therein, on the right side of the back: (4) *saṃ aṃ* salutation to the digit Pūṣā. On the back of the right shoulder: (4) *sāṃ āṃ* salutation to the digit Vaśā. On the back of the right neck: (4) *siṃ iṃ* salutation to the digit Sumanā.
In the right ear (4): *sīṃ īṃ* salutation to Ratikalā. In the right eye (4): *su uṃ* salutation to Prītikalā.
In the right nose (4): *sūṃ ūṃ* salutation to Dhṛtikalā. In the right forehead (4): *sṛṃ ṛṃ* salutation to Ṛddhikalā. On the right crown (4): *sṛṃ ṝṃ* salutation to Saumyākalā.
On the left head: *stṛṃ ḷṃ* to Marīcikalā; on the left forehead: *sṝṃ ḹṃ* to Aṃśumālinīkalā; on the left nostril: *seṃ aiṃ* to Aṅgirākalā; on the left eye:
*saiṃ aiṃ* to Śaśinīkalā; on the left ear: *soṃ oṃ* to Chāyākalā.
On the back of the left neck: *sauṃ auṃ* to the digit *Saṃpūrṇamaṇḍalā*.
On the back of the left shoulder: *saṃ aṃ* to the digit *Tuṣṭi*. On the left side of the back:
*saḥ aḥ* salutation to the digit *Amṛtā*. These sixteen [deities] are to be meditated upon as white, holding blue lotuses in their hands.
The placement of the lunar digits (somakalā-nyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight goddesses of speech, beginning with Vaśinī.

There, on the head: (4) *aṃ āṃ* (14) *vlū*, obeisance to Vaśinī Vāgdevatā. On the forehead: (4) *kaṃ* (4) *kalahrīṃ*, obeisance to Kāmeśvarī Vāgdevatā. Between the eyebrows: (4) *ca* (0) (4) *nvlīṃ*, obeisance to Modinī Vāgdevatā. At the throat: (4) *ṭaṃ* (0) (4) *plūṃ*, obeisance to Vimalā Vāgdevatā. At the heart: (4) *taṃ* (0) (4).
JMRĪṂ, to the Dawn-colored Goddess of Speech (na). At the navel: PAṂ HASALVYŪṂ, to the Victorious Goddess of Speech. At the *mūlādhāra*: YAṂ SAMARAYŪṂ, to the Sovereign of All Goddess of Speech.
From the *mūlādhāra* to the ends of the two feet: (4) *śaṃ* (5) *kṣmrīṃ*, salutation to Kaulinī Vāgdevatā. Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of Vāgdevatā.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four seats (catuḥpīṭha).

There, having uttered the first *kūṭa* at the *mūlādhāra*, [one offers] salutation to the goddess Śrī Kāmeśvarī— the Rudra-form energy (*rudrātmaśakti*) consisting of the power of will (*icchāśakti*), presiding over the waking state, whose essence is Lord Mitreśa, located in the fire-wheel (*agnicakra*) at the seat (*pīṭha*) of Kāmagiri. Then, having uttered the second *kūṭa* at the heart, [one offers] salutation to the goddess Bhagamālinī— the Śiva-form energy (*śivātmaśakti*) consisting of the power of action (*kriyāśakti*), presiding over the dreaming state, located in the sun-wheel (*sūryacakra*).

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Vajreśvarī, who is of the nature of the power of knowledge (jñāna-śakti), whose essence is Viṣṇu, who presides over the state of dream, and who is the very self of Ṣaṣṭhīśanātha at the sacred seat (pīṭha) of Jālandhara.
Having uttered the third peak-syllable (kūṭa) in the center of the eyebrows, [one should contemplate her] in the lunar wheel (soma-cakra) at the sacred seat of Pūrṇagiri.

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Bhagamālinī, who is of the nature of Uḍḍīśanātha, who presides over the state of deep sleep (*suṣupti*), and who is the power of the Self that is Brahman, consisting of the power of action (*kriyā-śakti*). Having uttered the Turyavidyā in the *brahmarandhra*, [one should worship] in the *brahmacakra* at the seat of Uḍḍiyāṇa, which is of the nature of Śrī Caryānātha.

Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, the power of the Self who is the Supreme Brahman, the presiding deity of the state beyond the fourth (turyātīta). Thus ends the Nyāsa of the Four Seats (catuḥpīṭha).
Now follows the placement (*nyāsa*) of Kāmeśvarī and the others.

Therein, from the big toe of the left foot up to the navel: (4) *Aiṃ*, salutation to Kāmeśvarī, the first peak-syllable (*kūṭa*). From the navel up to the throat: (4) *Klīṃ*, the second peak-syllable.
Salutation to Vajreśvarī. From the throat to the head, [placing] the third *kūṭa*,
"sauḥ," [with the words] "salutation to Bhagamālinī"— having thus performed the placement on the left side,
[one should place] from the big toe of the right foot to the navel [the syllable] "hasaiṃ" [with the words] "to Brahmā, the lord of the Ātma-tattva."

*Namaḥ*. From the navel to the throat: (4) *has klīṃ*, salutation to Viṣṇu, the lord of the principle of knowledge (*vidyā-tattva*). From the throat to the head: (4) *has auḥ*, salutation to Rudra, the lord of the principle of Śiva (*śiva-tattva*). Thus ends the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the deities of the principles.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the four principles (catustattva).

The first *kūṭa* (from the navel to the feet): (4) *Ātmatattvātmane śrīmahātripurasundaryai namaḥ*. The second *kūṭa* (from the throat to the navel): (4) *Vidyātattvātmane śrīmahātripurasundaryai namaḥ*. [The third *kūṭa*] (from the head to the throat): (4) ...

To the third peak, the essence of the Śiva-tattva, the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, obeisance! Reciting the fourth Vidyā (4) from the head down to the feet, [one should say]: "To the essence of all the tattvas, the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, obeisance! Thus one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*). This is the ritual placement of the four principles (*catustattvanyāsa*).
Now, the placement of the root-mantra (mūlavidyānyāsa): at the mūlādhāra.

(4) The first peak-syllable at the heart; (4) the second peak-syllable *namaḥ* between the eyebrows; (4) the third peak-syllable *namaḥ* in the aperture of Brahmā. Having thus deposited the fourth vidyā in the aperture of Brahmā, one should deposit the entire vidyā as a pervasive [covering], as before. Thus it is said.
The placement of the Root-Vidyā (*mūlavidyānyāsa*). And that must be performed with the *bālā* [vidyā] alone. It is as follows: *aiṃ namaḥ* on the left ear;

*klīṃ namaḥ* on the right ear; *sauḥ namaḥ* on the chin. In this manner, the second *yoni* is on the left temple, the right temple, and the mouth. The third [yoni] is on the left eye, the right eye, and the nose.

The fourth [syllable] is placed on the left shoulder, the right shoulder, and the heart; the fifth on the left elbow, the right elbow, and the navel; the sixth on the left knee, the right knee, and the penis; the seventh on the left foot, the right foot, and the anus;
the eighth on the left side, the right side, and the chest; the ninth on the left breast, the right breast, and the throat. Thus.
The external placement of the nine wombs (bahirnavayoninyāsa).
Now follows the internal placement (nyāsa) of the nine wombs (yonis).

Therein, in the nine locations beginning with the *mūlādhāra* and extending to the forehead, the *sīmantam*, and the *brahmarandhra*, one should mentally meditate upon and perform the internal placement (*nyāsa*) of the three previously mentioned seed-syllables (*bīja*), which are encircled by squares and arranged within nine triangles, proceeding clockwise from the southeast corner (*susvāgra*). Thus ends the internal placement of the nine triangles (*antarnavayoninyāsa*).

The Unchained Placement (*aśṛkhalānyāsa*). Therein, the first *kūṭa* with *namaḥ* is at the crest-lock (*śikhā*); likewise, the second at the chin (*cibuka*); the third at the mouth (*mukha*). Again, the first at the mouth; the second at the throat (*kaṇṭha*); the third at the chin. Again, the first at the chin; the second at the heart (*hṛdaya*); [the third] at the throat.

The third peak-syllable. Again, the first peak-syllable at the throat; the second at the navel; the third at the heart. Again, the first at the heart; the second at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; the third at the navel. Again, the first at the navel.

The second [syllable] at the *mūlādhāra*; the third at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*. Again, the first at the *svādhiṣṭhāna*; the second on the thighs; the third at the *mūlādhāra*. This is the *śṛkhalā-nyāsa* (chain-binding ritual placement). Next is the *aprakaṭa-nyāsa* (unmanifest ritual placement).

And there, at the *mūlādhāra*: (4) *aṃ āṃ sauṃḥ*, salutation to the manifest yoginīs (*prakaṭayoginī*) residing in the wheel that fascinates the three worlds (*trailokyamohanacakra*). At the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: (4) *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*, salutation to the secret yoginīs (*guptayoginī*) residing in the wheel that fulfills all desires (*sarvāśāparipūraka*). At the *maṇipūraka*: (4) *jñīṃ klīṃ sauḥ*.

Salutation to the most secret Yoginīs stationed in the Sarvasaṃkṣobhaṇa-cakra; at the heart: (4) *haiṃ hakalī hasauḥ*, salutation to the Saṃpradāya Yoginīs stationed in the Sarvasaubhāgyadāyaka-cakra;
at the Viśuddhi [cakra]: (4) *haṃsai hasakalīṃ hasauḥ*, [salutation] to those stationed in the Sarvārthasādhaka-cakra.

Salutation to the Kulakaula yogis! At the Ājñā [cakra] (4): *hrīṃ klīṃ bleṃ rarva*, salutation to the Nigarbha Yoginīs residing in the protection-bestowing wheel (*rakṣākara-cakra*). At the forehead (4): *hrīṃ śrīṃ sauḥ*, salutation to the Rahasya Yoginīs residing in the disease-removing wheel (*sarvarogahara-cakra*). At the head (4): *hasaiṃ*.

*Hasakalarīṃ hasrauḥ*, salutation to the Yoginīs of the supreme and non-supreme secret, who abide in the wheel that bestows all accomplishments (*sarvasiddhipradacakrasthābhyah*). Having recited the fifteenth root mantra (*mūlapañcadaśī*) at the *brahmarandhra*: "Salutation to the Yoginīs of the supreme and non-supreme most secret [wheel], who abide in the wheel consisting of universal bliss (*sarvānandamayacakrasthābhyah parāparātira hasyayoginībhyo namaḥ*). Having thus performed the placement (*vinyasya*), [recite] *samasta*...

With the mantra beginning with *prakaṭā* and so forth, one should perform the placement (*nyāsa*) that pervades all limbs by means of the collective Vidyā of the Yoginīs; this is the *Prakaṭādi-nyāsa*.
Now follows the *Amaṭha-nyāsa*.

There, on the head: (4) Oṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ. On the forehead: (4) Hrīṃ pārvatyai namaḥ. On the right eye: (4) Aṃ savitre namaḥ. On the left eye: (4) Aṃ agnaye namaḥ. On the perimeter of the mouth: (4) Ṭhaṃ candramase namaḥ. On the mouth: (4) Śrīṃ śriyai namaḥ. On the two cheeks: (4) Svāṃ hāṃ daṃtine namaḥ.
Thus ends the placement of the monasteries (amaṭha-nyāsa).
Now follows the fruit of this placement.
Whoever [performs this] three times at each of the three periods of the day, or five times, or seven times;
Or one may perform it tenfold; now hear its fruit, O Śivā. (1)
Beauty, intelligence, fame, happiness, and prosperity arise for him.
By Śrī Vidyānandanātha, the beloved son of Śiva and Śivā.
Thus, in the ocean of the jewels of good fortune, the eighth wave has arisen. (1)
[Thus ends the eighth wave in the *Saubhāgyaratnākara*, composed by Śrī Śrīvidyānandanātha, a resident at the pair of lotus feet of the venerable Saccidānandanātha. (2)
Now, the placement of the hoods (*phaṇānyāsa*):

Having meditated upon the lotus of vowels marked by the *a*-group in the pericarp of the four-petalled lotus at the *ādhāra*, and having visualized the *kuṇḍalinī* there endowed with hoods, one should place the first *kūṭa* on those hoods.
Having mentally arranged [the seed-syllable] in five colors.

Then, having visualized a lotus marked with the *ka*-group in the same manner within the pericarp of the twelve-petalled lotus of the *anāhata* [cakra], and having meditated upon her there endowed with seasonal hoods, one should place the second *kūṭākṣara* syllables upon the jewels of those hoods. Then, having visualized a lotus marked with the *tha*-group in the same manner within the *hakṣa*-lotus, one should meditate there.
Having meditated upon that [Goddess] as endowed with [her] purifiers and having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) there of the syllables of the *Śaktikūṭa*,

one should then meditate on a lotus of letters within the pericarp of the thousand-petaled lotus; having visualized her there as possessing fifteen hoods, one should perform the placement of the root-syllables there— this is the placement of the hoods (*phaṇānyāsa*).
Now, the Sarvasaṃmohana Nyāsa: On the head:
(4) *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to Nāda-nāda. On the forehead: (4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hasakalarīṃ*, salutation to Śūnya-nāda. Between the eyebrows: (4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ ka e*... [text truncated]

*Ilhrīṃ*, salutation to the Unmodified Sound (*avikṛtanāda*); on the nose: (4) *hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃ sakalahrīṃ*, salutation to the Tactile Sound (*sparśanāda*). On the mouth: (4) *hsīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the Resonant Sound (*dhvanināda*). On the heart: (4) *aṃ āṃ sauṃ aiṃ hsauṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ*, salutation to the Sound-of-Sound (*nādanāda*). On the belly: (4) ...

*Īhasakalhrīṃ ka e il hrīṃ aiṃ klīṃ sauṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bindunādāya namaḥ* | At the navel (4): *īha sakala hrīṃ śrīṃ vikṛtinādāya namaḥ* | At the root (4): *hsauṃ sauṃ sakala hrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ bījanādāya namaḥ* | At the *mūlādhāra* (4): *oṃ haṃ saḥ hrīṃ śrīṃ*
Salutation to Akṣaranāda. (4) One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka-nyāsa) over the entire body with the root mantra;
this is the Sarvasaṃmohana-nyāsa.
Now follows the secret sixfold placement (guhya-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa).
It is as follows:
Śaṅkara said:
It is now stated what [must be practiced] so that mantras do not succeed in the Kali age without it.
By this, the mantra-tantras are certainly accomplished instantly. (1)
O Rāvaṇa, the seed was previously sown by the Rākṣasas through that continuity.
And one should also perform the ritual placements (nyāsa) for these means of accomplishment in their proper sequence. (2)
However, there are the Vidyās, the Mahāvidyās, and likewise the Gaṇeśa-mantras.
And the Hayagrīva mantra itself is declared to be the seed-syllable on this earth. (3)

Oṃ. Of this Nyāsa of the Sixfold Śrī Guhya Śrī Mahācakreśvarī, Dakṣiṇāmūrti is the Seer (Ṛṣi), Anuṣṭubh is the Metre (Chandas), Śrī Mahātripurasundarī is the Deity (Devatā), Sāṅkhyāyana is the Lineage (Gotra), Aiṃ is the Seed-syllable (Bīja), Hrīṃ is the Power (Śakti), and Klīṃ is the Bolt (Kīlaka). [This is for the purpose of attaining success through the grace of the Guru and the Deity.]
The application for the secret sixfold placement (*guhya-ṣoḍhānyāsa*):
(4) *Aiṃ* to the two middle fingers, *namaḥ*. (4) *Hrīṃ* to the two ring fingers, *namaḥ*. (4) *Śrīṃ* to the two little fingers, *namaḥ*.
(4) *Aiṃ* to the two thumbs, *namaḥ*. (4) *Hrīṃ* to the two index fingers, *namaḥ*.
*Śrīṃ* to both palms and backs of the hands. Having thus performed the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) beginning with the heart:
*(4)* *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hsraiṃ hasakalīṃ hsauṃḥ* to Tripurā, *namaḥ*, on the crest-lock (*śikhā*). *(4)* *Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ* to Bālātripurā, *namaḥ*, on the mouth. *(4)* *Aiṃ* to Śāradātripurā, *namaḥ*.

At the throat: (4) *kṣrauṃ śrīṃ kṣrau* obeisance to Siddheśvarī. At the forehead: (4) *hasrauṃ hasraklīṃ hsrauḥ* obeisance to Tripurāsiddhā. Between the eyebrows: (4) *hsrauṃ hsklīṃ hsrauḥ* obeisance to Tripurāparameśvarī. At the neck: (4) [The same mantra as above].

Kāmarājavidyā (15): *Namaḥ* to Rājarājeśvarī at the heart. (4) *Na pha kṣma la va yūṃ*: *Namaḥ* to Mālinī Tripurā above the heart. (4) Lopāmudrāvidyā (15): *Namaḥ* to Goddess Tripurasundarī above the anus. (4) *Hasarīṃ hasarīṃ śṛṃ*: *Namaḥ* to the bliss-bestowing Tripurā at the penis. (4) *Klīṃ*.

Kāmeśvaryai namaḥ on the secret place. (4) Hrīṃ Tripurabhu-vaneśvaryai namaḥ on all the limbs. (4) Haṃ Saḥ Nirvāṇasundaryai namaḥ on the nostril aperture. (4) Hrīṃ Hsrauṃ Śrauṃ Haripriyāparamāryai namaḥ on the Brahma-aperture. (4) Aiṃ (15) Pañcadaśī Nakṣatra Vallabhāyai.

*Namo* on the forehead. (4) *Klīṃ*, the peak-syllable of Kāmarāja, *namo ratipriyāyai* on the two ears. (4) *Hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ*, *namaḥ śakrapriyāyai* on the nose. (4) *Kūṃ sauṃ*, the peak-syllable of Lopāmudrā and others, *namaḥ śambhupriyāyai* on the lips. (4) *Aiṃ*, *namaḥ prāṇeśvaryai*.
Salutation to the two rows of teeth. (4) Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Sauḥ, salutation to Jīveśvarī on the tongue.
(4) Hrīṃ Śrīṃ, salutation to Brahmāṇī on the two elbows. (4) Haṃsaḥ Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Hūṃ So'haṃ, salutation to her whose nature is the Supreme Self on the back. Oṃ (3) Oṃ Sṛṃ Hṛṃ.

*Sauḥ*, salutation to the one whose form is the Earth, on all limbs. (4) Having uttered the sixteenth [syllable], *hrīṃ*, salutation to Hṛllekhā, at the heart. *Oṃ* (3) *sauṃḥ klī* (3), salutation to Bhṛgupriyā, at the breasts. (4) Salutation to the one whose form is Wrath, at the belly. (4) *Śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ saḥ*, salutation to the goddess Vitākā, at the *liṅga*. (4) *hrīṃ*.

*klīṃ* obeisance to Bhuvaneśvarī; from the head down to the feet. (4) *aiṃ* obeisance to Vāgbhairavī at the *mūlādhāra*. (4) *klīṃ* obeisance to Kāmarūpā below the heart. (4) *sauṃḥ* obeisance to Śaktibhagā at the forehead. *oṃ* (3) [to] Samasta...
Having recited the root mantra: "Obeisance to the venerable Mahātripurasundarī," one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) over all limbs.
Then, as before, one should perform the six-limbed ritual (*ṣaḍaṅga*) on the hands.
O Great Goddess, whoever performs this ritual placement day and night,
He indeed attains perfection; for him, liberation is certain. (1)
There is neither old age nor death, nor any fear of kings and the like.
Whoever deposits this deposit is liberated; of this there is no doubt. (2)
And one should assign the thirty-two great vidyās to the aforementioned locations.
The placement of Mahācakreśvarī is difficult even for the gods to achieve. (3)
