She who holds a skull-topped staff, the one of great power, who carries one across the ocean of worldly existence.
She who is proclaimed among all mantras as the Speaker of Mantras (Mantravādinī).
And she who is called Kālaghnī, the Supreme Goddess at the end of the age.
She is proclaimed as "The Seizer" by the gods, asuras, and great serpents.
She who is called Cakriṇī is also Ekapādā and Trilocanā.
She who is the goddess Viśvabāhukā, who is always beloved by Viśvanātha.
That [is it]. (53) ||
Bhuvaneśvarī is known throughout all the philosophical systems.
In the treatise, that which is known as Kaṇṭakī is intended for the purpose of cutting through thorns.
She who is called Kīlikī is seven cubits tall and possesses great strength.
She who is called Mahāmārī, the Great Goddess in battle.
She who is renowned as Yamadūtī is worshipped by both gods and demons.
The goddess who is Karālinī is Mahāmāyā, possessed of great power.
The Great Queen Lalitāmbā is the sole leader of the entire wheel.
Kaulinī should abide at the tip of the nose, and likewise Madanākṣī in the mouth.
She who is born from the sky, she who dwells in the skull, and she who captivates even the palate. (61)
The Drāviṇī, the Kṣobhiṇī, the Staṃbhinī, and likewise the Mohinī.
Raudrakarmā, Mahāghaṇṭā, Ḍāmari, Tvaritā, and Mati. (62)
May the Goddess protect my body, and may the Mistress of the Clan protect my head.
Earth, water, fire, air, and space as well; (63)
May the Mistress of the Elements protect my family at all times within the five elements.
May the daughter of Indra grant me sovereignty, and may she be prolific with offspring. (64)
May Māyā grant me constantly wealth, grain, and likewise fame.
In battle, in the royal court, and even in the midst of enemies, O great hero! (65)
May the Great Goddess with blood-red eyes fulfill my intention.
One should guard the time and the non-time; the Vidyā [is preserved] through the Vidyā in the Kula tradition. (66)
O Lord of the World, she bestows upon practitioners the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Dvijaṭī and Trijaṭī are mentioned; Kaṃdalī is beloved by all. (67)
Gāyatrī, Ambikā, Tārā, Pārvatī, Kamalā, and Prabhā.
Mādinī, Madanodbhāvā, Mandārī, and Madanāturā. (68)
Named Bhīṣaṇābhīṣaṇī, she is a ghost perfected in sorcery and is terrifying.
Hunger, thirst, as well as sleep, luster, growth, and radiance—(69).
The twilight observance, night, and patience are indeed recited as being constant, day and night.
In that city, she was renowned as Suranāthā, a deity among men. (70)
For they know the Goddess Grā to be the presiding deity, the Mistress of the Pīṭha in every pīṭha.
The Kāverī is indeed the Narmadā, and the Gaṅgā is called the Yamunā. (71)
The Godāvarī is declared to be greatly meritorious, as is Arundhatī.
Even in the three worlds, no woman has been revealed who is equal to the Great Goddess by name. (72)
That goddess shall abide within my heart, the essence of Śrī, which possesses a hundred thousand forms.
It is indeed declared that this knowledge is called Suvarṇarekhinī. (73)
May she, who uproots the serpents, grant me happiness.
She became renowned as Kuru-kullā, born from the mouth of the King of Birds. (74)
That Vidyā, who is of great form, may she always abide upon the tip of my tongue.
May she who is renowned as Oṃkāriṇī always abide within my body. (75)
She is named the Remover of Obstacles, the Destroyer of the Form of Kali.
May Bhetaṇḍā abide in my throat; may Totalā abide on my head. (76)
So that even a very small line may always remain at my root.
May she grant me the perfection of speech for the destruction of wild poisons. (77)
This vidyā brings about all accomplishments and bestows the fruits of both worldly enjoyment and liberation.
I am Brahmā, I am Viṣṇu, and I am the god Maheśvara.
I am the abode of all beings, the Lord of the World, and the contemplator of Śakti. (78)
With their bodies purified by the placement of the Śaktis, the gods and demons [attained success].
Having been granted [this] by the mere mention of the region, may you always carry out my command. (79)
O Śaṅkara, whatever form of Yoginī exists even within the three worlds, [is she not you?].
All that remains within the body when the ritual placement of power (*śaktinyāsa*) has been practiced. (80)
And the passionate woman also performs the ritual placement (nyāsa) fashioned by Śakti.
They know that goddess of divine form to be Tripurā within saṃsāra. (81)
Salutations to you, O Mother of Birth; salutations to you, O Sovereign of the World.
Salutations to the goddess who bestows enjoyments; salutations to the goddess Maheśvarī. (82)
She is both manifest and hidden, entirely extinguished, Bhairavī, and auspicious.
She is Sambhramā, Vijayā, Haṃsā, Śubhā, and that goddess of the waters. (83)
The yakṣiṇī Cūḍā and likewise the maiden Ākāśagāminī.
She who moves upon the earth, she who dwells in the water-jar, and she who resides in all the Agamas. (84)
Raṅginī is Devamaitrī, and she is renowned as Madirālikā.
She is worshipped for the sake of all accomplishments in this scripture of the Yoginī-mata. (85)
She who dwells in the forest is called Nandā by the virtuous.
By whom the sixty-four Yoginīs of Āśrayadevī were meditated upon. (86)
When [the elements] dissolve into the foundation (ādhāra), that yogi becomes a knower of yoga.
May Maṇḍalā abide on the forehead; may Virajā abide on the head. (87)
She has one eye on her right shoulder and three eyes on her left.
May Jayantī remain in my belly, and Kandarpakuṇḍalī at my waist. (88)
Mālinī resides at the junction of the liṅgas, and Samādhinī abides in the heart.
Ambikā shall stand upon the spinal column, and Medinī upon the two sides. (89)
Diggajantī is at the tips of the fingers, and Nāgendrī is at the joints of the nails.
The tiger and the discus are located on the shanks, while the earth is at the feet. (90)
Amṛtā is in the aperture, and Vilāsinī is in the eyes.
May Kālindī protect the root-tongue, and may Raktinī protect the blood. (91)
Lāṅgalī protects the wilderness, and asthinī [protects] the joints of the bones.
Majjinī is the marrow of the body, and Śukreśvarī is likewise the semen. (92)
And may you, Vetālī, the destroyer of my disease, protect me.
Udbhaṭā always brings peace to my body. (93)
May she stand at my feet and at the soles of my feet; may she, the traveler, protect me on the path.
May Bhairavī protect [us] from fear of thieves, fire, kings, and serpents. (94)
May Bandhinī always effect the binding of the vision of the wicked.
May that Cāpeṭīnī vidyā grant me auspiciousness. (95)
Markaṭī, Ghaṇṭakarṇī, Hanumatī, and Rāvaṇī.
I salute the fourfold sciences, renowned for their fame as the Ghurghurī. (96)
Ceṭakā, Jñānadā, Vidyā, Kaumārī, and Caraṇāvalī.
Named Vighnarājastutā, she consists of the fourfold continuum of emanations. (97)
The female swan (Haṃsī) resides in the primordial space (mūlākāśa), exalted by the shattering of the petals of sin.
May these ten mantra-sciences abide upon my head. (98)
Śubhā shall stand in front, and Lohitā shall stand on the right.
And at the time of sexual union, Śṛṅkhalā should stand on the left side in the western direction. (99)
Śaṅkhinī shall protect the crest-lock, and the auspicious Vastravatī shall protect the garment.
She who possesses armor in her armor and who has made a festival for her eyes in her eyes. (100)
They abide in the form of Yoginīs throughout the three worlds, including all that is mobile and immobile.
May all those Yoginīs who have been praised make my body their abode. (101)
Likewise, it should be given to one's sons, and especially to those who are devoted.
This Śaktinyāsa should not be given to just anyone, O God. (102)
It bestows the fruit of whatever goals are desired by human beings in the world of mortals.
O Lord, he who performs my nyāsa, such as the ṣoḍhā-nyāsa and others— (103) ||
Indeed, while living, he is the very form of power, capable of uprooting the three worlds.
When the *śaktinyāsa* has been performed upon the living being, whoever might be a cutter [of it], (104) ||
Through action, mind, or speech, he will experience remorse.
O Śaṅkara, this installation of the powers (śaktinyāsa), which is dear to me, has been declared to you. (105)
By means of that which is applied to the body, a person becomes equal to Śakti.
When enraged, the yogi can bring about even the downfall of the three worlds. (106)
O Śaṅkara, the hero is endowed with the placement of the powers (śaktinyāsa) through the act of salutation.
It causes a bursting to occur directly in stone images and the like. (107)
Thus ends the ritual placement of the powers (śakti-nyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the root-mantra consisting of sixteen syllables of Śrī.

There, having meditated upon Śrīvidyā— who is shaped like a lamp, resides in the *brahmaraṃdhra*, bestows great good fortune, and causes nectar to flow from the syllables of the mantra, thereby bathing her own body with that nectar—
one should [place] the *praṇava* and the *tritārā* etc. at the *brahmaraṃdhra* with the middle and ring fingers of the right hand.
One should place the root-vidyā ending with "namaḥ. (1)

Again, having uttered that [mantra] and having formed the *saubhāgyadaṇḍinī* mudrā with the left hand, one should whirl it around the region of the left ear and install the Vidyā in the same manner upon the left side of the body, from the head down to the feet, while reciting: "Grant me great good fortune; I shall punish the good fortune of others."
Having firmly formed a fist with the left hand, one should extend the index finger.
One should rotate [the hand] from the left ear; this mudrā is Saubhāgyadaṇḍinī. (1)
In the same way, having again uttered that [mantra] and thinking, "I shall subdue my enemies," one should display the *ripujihvāgraha* mudrā and place it at the base of the feet. (3)
One should form a fist with the left hand, with the thumb tucked inside.
This mudrā, called Ripujihvāgraha, is said to be the destroyer of enemies. (1)

In the same manner, having uttered that [mantra], while meditating "I am the creator of the three worlds," one should place it as a tilaka on the forehead by means of the *trikhaṇḍā* mudrā. (4) In the same manner, having uttered that [mantra], one should place it around the face as a binding. (5) In the same manner, having uttered that [mantra], [one should place it] around the face from the right ear to the left ear.
One should perform the placement (vinyāsa). (6) Again, in the same manner, one should place that [syllable] from the throat to the mouth. (7)
Again, in that same manner, she [spoke].

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) from the soles of the feet up to the crown of the head, and from the top of the head down to the heart, all enclosed by the *praṇava* (Oṃ), and having formed the *yonimudrā* and cast [the mantra] into the mouth with the root-vidyā, one should likewise prostrate. Thus ends the *Śrīvidyāpūrṇajagadvaśīkaraṇanyāsa*.
(*) The ritual placement (nyāsa) for total delusion.

There, recollecting the sixteen-syllable Śrī-mantra and meditating on the Goddess by whose splendor the three worlds become crimson in color, one should rotate [the mantra] around the head and install it at the unnamed finger (the ring finger). (1)

Having performed the placement [of the mantra] at the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*) with the thumb and ring finger, using the sixteen-syllable Śrīvidyā mantra preceded by *Tārā* (Oṃ) and ending with *namaḥ*; (2) having performed it separately on both wrists; (4) and having placed it on the forehead with the ring finger; (5)—this is the Saṃmohana-nyāsa.
Now follows the Saṃhāra-nyāsa (dissolution placement) with the syllables of the glorious sixteen-syllable mantra.

Therein, on the two feet (4), the first seed-syllable *namaḥ*; on the two calves (4), the second *namaḥ*; on the two knees (4), the third *namaḥ*; on the two hips (4), the fourth *namaḥ*; on the penis (4), the fifth *namaḥ*; on the back (4), the sixth *namaḥ*; on the navel (4), the seventh; on the two sides (4), the eighth.
The ninth [syllable] is on the two breasts; the tenth is on the two shoulders; the eleventh is on the two ears.
The twelfth [syllable] at the aperture of Brahma (the crown of the head); the thirteenth on the face; the fourteenth on the linga;
the fifteenth near the two ear-lobes; and the sixteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the two ear-rings.
Thus is the placement of dissolution (saṃhāranyāsa) by means of the sixteen syllables.
Now follows the creation-assignment (sṛṣṭinyāsa) with sixteen syllables.

There, in the *brahmarandhra*, is the first seed-syllable: *namaḥ*. On the forehead is the second; on the two eyes is the third; on the two ears is the fourth; on the two nostrils is the fifth; on the two lips is the sixth;
between the teeth is the seventh; above the teeth is the eighth; and on the tongue is [the ninth].

The ninth [syllable] on the face; the tenth on the other mouth; the eleventh on the back; the twelfth on all the limbs; the thirteenth on the heart; the fourteenth on the two breasts; the fifteenth on the belly; and the sixteenth seed-syllable, *namaḥ*, on the *liṅga*. Having thus assigned the letters, [one should contemplate] the whole...
One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpakanyāsa) with the sixteen-syllable vidyā. Thus ends the placement of emanation (sṛṣṭinyāsa).
Now follows the placement of stability (sthitinyāsa) with those [same] syllables.

Therein, the first seed-syllable *namaḥ* is [placed] on the two thumbs of both hands; likewise, the second on the two index fingers; the third on the two middle fingers; the fourth on the two ring fingers;
the fifth on the two little fingers; the sixth in the aperture of Brahmā (*brahmarandhra*); the seventh in the mouth; and the eighth in the heart.
The ninth [concentration] is from the navel to the feet (4). The tenth is from the throat to the navel (4).

The eleventh is from the Brahma-aperture to the throat (4). The twelfth is on the two big toes (4). The thirteenth is on the two index fingers (4). The fourteenth is on the two middle fingers (4). The fifteenth is on the two ring fingers (4).
The fifteenth: that is the sixteenth seed-syllable *namaḥ* on the two little fingers. Thus is the placement for stability (*sthitinyāsa*).
Now follows the fivefold deposition of the letters for the venerable sixteen-syllable mantra.

On the head (4), the first seed-syllable: *namaḥ*. Likewise, on the mouth (4), the second: *namaḥ*. On the right eye (4), the third; on the left eye (4), the fourth; on the right ear (4), the fifth; on the left ear (4), the sixth; on the right nostril (4), the seventh; on the left nostril (4), the eighth.
On the right cheek (4), the ninth; on the left cheek (4), the tenth; on the upper lip (4), the eleventh; on the lower lip (4), the twelfth;
inside the mouth (4), the thirteenth; on the upper teeth (4), the fourteenth;
on the lower teeth (4), the fifteenth; in the face (4), the sixteenth seed-syllable is *namaḥ*. This is one method.

Therein, the first seed-syllable *namaḥ* is at the head; the second at the hairline (*sīmanta*); the third on the forehead (*bhāla*); the fourth between the two eyebrows; the fifth on the nose; the sixth on the face;
the seventh at the base of the right arm; the eighth at the joint in the middle of it; [and the ninth] at its wrist.

The ninth [syllable] at the base of those fingers; the tenth at their tips; the eleventh at the base of the left arm; the twelfth in its middle; the thirteenth at its wrist; the fourteenth at the base of those fingers; the fifteenth at their tips; the sixteenth seed-syllable is *namaḥ*. Thus ends the second [section].
The method: Then, first on the head; likewise, the second on the forehead; the third on the right eye; the fourth on the left eye; the fifth on the mouth; the sixth on the tip of the tongue;
the seventh at the root of the right thigh; the eighth on the knee; the ninth on its ankle; [and] on its toes.
At the base of the [right] foot (4), the tenth; at the tips of its toes (4), the eleventh; at the base of the left thigh (4), the twelfth;
at its knee (4), the thirteenth; at its ankle (4), the fourteenth; at the base of its toes (4), the fifteenth;
and at the tips of its toes (4), the sixteenth seed-syllable is *namaḥ*. This is the third method.
Therein, the first is on the head; the second on the circumference of the face; the third on the right eye; the fourth on the left; the fifth on the right ear; the sixth on the left ear;
the seventh on the right nostril; the eighth on the left nostril; the ninth on the right cheek; [the tenth] on the left cheek.

The tenth [syllable] on the upper lip; the eleventh on the lower lip; the twelfth on the upper teeth; the fourteenth on the lower teeth; the fifteenth on the crown of the head; the sixteenth, "namaḥ," on the tongue. This is the fourth method.
Then, the first [syllable] on the forehead; the second on the throat; the third on the heart; the fourth at the navel;
the fifth at the *mūlādhāra*; the sixth at the *brahmarandhra*; the seventh on the heart; the eighth at the *mūlādhāra*;
again, the ninth at the *mūlādhāra*; and the tenth on the heart.

In the *brahmarandhra* (4), the eleventh; on the palm of the right hand (4), the twelfth; on the palm of the left hand (4), the thirteenth; in the right foot, the fourteenth; in the left foot (4), the fifteenth; in the heart (4), the sixteenth: *namaḥ*. Thus ends the fifth method.

Having performed this placement (nyāsa) and having placed the sixteen-syllable Śrī-vidyā— enclosed by the Praṇava— as a pervasive covering over all limbs, one should then likewise place that same Vidyā in the heart. These nyāsas are to be performed only by those who worship the sixteen-syllable [Vidyā].
"Not by others"—this is the instruction of the Guru. Thus end the ritual placements (nyāsa), beginning with the purification of the hands.
By Śrī Vidyānandanātha, the beloved son of Śiva and Śivā.
Thus, the ninth wave in this ocean of the jewels of good fortune has come to an end. (1)
[Thus ends the ninth wave in the Saubhāgyaratnākara composed by Śrī Śrīvidyānandanātha, who dwells at the pair of lotus feet of the venerable Saccidānandanātha. (9)
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the Upper Tradition (ūrdhvāmnāya).
And that is threefold: the Great Sixfold Installation (mahāṣoḍhānyāsa),
the installation of the sixteen Root-Mantras beginning with Śaṃcaraṇa and the six supports (ṣaḍādhāra-mūlavidyā-nyāsa),
and the installation of the Ṣaḍanvaya-Śāmbhava.

In this regard, those initiated into the *ūrdhvāmnāya* by means of the supreme grace (*parā-prasāda*) have authority only for the *mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa*. Those initiated into the *vidyā* [initiation] by means of the *caraṇa* and so forth have authority only for the *nyāsa*s beginning with that [the *caraṇa*], but not for the *mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa*. However, those initiated by both types [of initiation] have authority in all cases.

Therein, first is the Great Sixfold Deposition (*mahāṣoḍhānyāsa*). Regarding this venerable Great Sixfold Deposition: Brahmā is the seer (*ṛṣi*), Jagatī is the meter (*chandas*), and the venerable Ardhanārīśvara is the deity (*devatā*). Its application (*viniyoga*) is in the deposition as a limb of the Śrīvidyā. Thus [is] the seer and so forth.

Having performed the placement (*nyāsa*) upon the crown of the head and other parts by means of mindfulness, one should perform the limb-placement (*aṅganyāsa*). The limb-placement consists of [the assignment] to the fingers and the body-face.
Therein, first is the assignment of the fingers (*aṅgulinyāsa*).
There, on the two thumbs: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauḥ śauṃḥ hoṃ*—salutation to Īśāna.
On the two index fingers: (4) (2) *heṃ* to Tatpuruṣa, obeisance. On the two middle fingers: (4) (2) *huṃ* to Aghora, obeisance. On the two ring fingers:
(4) (2) *hīṃ* to Vāmadeva, obeisance. On the two little fingers: (4) (2) *haṃ* to Sadyojāta, obeisance. (1)
On the head (4): (2) *hoṃ īśānāya namaḥ*. On the face (4): (2) *heṃ tatpuruṣāya namaḥ*.
On the heart (4): (2) *huṃ aghorāya namaḥ*. On the secret place (4): (2) *hiṃ vāmadevāya namaḥ*. On the two feet (4):
(2) *haṃ sadyojātāya namaḥ*. || (2) ||

On the crown of the head (4): (2) *Hoṃ*, salutation to Īśāna, the upper face. On the mouth (4): (2) *Heṃ*, salutation to Tatpuruṣa, the eastern face. On the right ear (4): (2) *Hūṃ*, salutation to Aghora, the southern face. On the left ear (4): (2) *Hīṃ*, salutation to Vāmadeva, the northern face.
At the Thieves' Well (4): (2) "Haṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta, the western face. Thus is the ritual placement on the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).

This is the placement of the five faces (*pañcavaktranyāsa*): one should place each face sequentially upon each of the five fingers, beginning with the thumb. Thus is the placement of the limbs (*aṅganyāsa*).
Then, having performed the purification of the hands and the six-limbed placement (*kara-ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*) using *hasāṃ*, *hasīṃ*, and so forth, [one proceeds].
Having meditated upon the deity in the form that will be described hereafter within one's heart, one should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa).
Therein, first is the *prapañca-nyāsa*.
It is as follows: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ aṃ* to Śrī, who is the form of the manifold universe (*prapañca-rūpā*), obeisance. Thus it is everywhere. (6)
Āṃ, salutation to Māyā, who has the form of an island; (6) Iṃ, salutation to Kamalā, who has the form of the ocean;

(6) Īṃ, salutation to Viṣṇuvallabhā, who has the form of a mountain; (6) Uṃ, salutation to Padmadhāriṇī, who has the form of a city; (6) Ūṃ, salutation to Samudratanayā, who has the form of a sacred seat (pīṭha); (6) Ṛṃ, [salutation] to her who has the form of a field (kṣetra).
To Lokamātā; (6) Ṛṃ, salutation to Rūpā, the dweller in the lotus;
(6) Ḷṃ, to Indirā, who has the form of a hermitage; (6) Ḹṃ, to Māyā, who has the form of a cave;
(6) Eṃ, to Ramā, who has the form of a river; (6) Aiṃ, to Padmā, who has the form of a crossroads; (6) Oṃ, to [the goddess] who has the form of that which is born from a sprout.

To her who is dear to Nārāyaṇa; (6) Oṃ, salutation to Siddhalakṣmī, whose form is born of sweat; (6) Aṃ, salutation to Rājalakṣmī, whose form is born of an egg; (6) Aḥ, salutation to Mahālakṣmī, whose form is born of a womb; (6) Kaṃ, salutation to Āryā, whose form is lava; (6) Khaṃ, salutation to Umā, whose form is truṭi; (6) Gaṃ...

To Caṇḍikā, whose form is the *kalā* [unit of time], (0); to Durgā, whose form is the *kāṣṭhā*, (6); to Śivā, whose form is the *nimeṣa*, (6); to Aparṇā, whose form is the *śvāsa* [breath], (6); to Ambikā, whose form is the *ghaṭikā*, (6); to Satī, whose form is the *muhūrta*, (6); to Jhaṃ... (6).
To Īśvarī, whose form is the watch of the day; (6) to Śāmbhavī, whose form is the day;
(6) to Īśānī, whose form is the twilight; (6) to Pārvatī, whose form is the night; (6) to Sarvamaṅgalā, whose form is the lunar day; (6) to Dākṣāyaṇī, whose form is the day of the week; (6) to Ṇaṃ.
To Nakṣatrarūpā Haimavatī; (6) to Yogarūpā Mahāmāyā; (6) to Karaṇarūpā Māheśvarī; (6) to Pakṣarūpā Mṛḍānī;
(6) to Māsarūpā Rudrāṇī; (6) to Rāśirūpā Śarvāṇī. (6)

Paṃ to the Supreme Sovereign (*parameśvarī*) who is the form of the seasons; Phaṃ to Kālī who is the form of the solstices (*ayana*); Baṃ to Kātyāyanī who is the form of the year (*saṃvatsara*); Bhaṃ to Gaurī who is the form of the ages (*yuga*); Maṃ to Bhavānī who is the form of dissolution (*pralaya*); Yaṃ to Brāhmī who is the form of the five elements (*pañcabhūta*); Raṃ...
To Vāgīśvarī, who is the form of the five subtle elements (*tanmātra*), *laṃ*; to Vāṇī, who is the form of the five organs of action (*karmendriya*), *vaṃ*;
to Sāvitrī, who is the form of the five organs of knowledge (*jñānendriya*), *śaṃ*;
to Sarasvatī, who is the form of the five vital breaths (*prāṇa*), *ṣaṃ*; to Gāyatrī, who is the form of the three qualities (*guṇa*), *saṃ*.

Salutation to the one whose form is the fourfold internal organ (*antaḥkaraṇa*), who bestows speech; (6) *haṃ*, salutation to Śāradā, whose form is the three states (*avasthā*); (6) *laṃ*, salutation to Bhāratī, whose form is the seven constituents (*dhātu*); (6) *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ kṣaṃ*, salutation to the one whose nature is knowledge (*vidyātmikā*), whose form is the three defects (*doṣatraya*).

Having thus deposited these fifty-one powers (*śakti*) in the locus of the Mother-letters (*mātṛkā*), one should then recite the *mātṛkā* from the letter *a* to the letter *kṣa*: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ*, and offer salutation: "Salutation to the Goddess Śrī Parāmbā, the presiding deity of the entire phenomenal world (*prapañca*)."
*Śauṃḥ hasauṃḥ śrī hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ*; one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) upon all limbs. Thus ends the *prapañcanyāsa*.
Now follows the assignment of the worlds (bhuvananyāsa).

There, on the two feet: *Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauḥ śauṃḥ aṃ āṃ iṃ*, obeisance to the Mother Goddess Ādhāraśakti, who resides in the world of Atala and is joined with the primordial deity (mūladevatā) known as the hundred-million Guhyā yoginīs.
At the two feet (6): *īṃ uṃ ūṃ*, O Root [Deity], the most secret infinite Yoginī residing in the hundred million worlds of Vitala;
At the two shanks (6): *ṛṃ ṝṃ ḷṃ*, O Root [Deity], the inconceivable and extremely secret Yoginī residing in the hundred million worlds of Sutala;
At the two knees (6): *ḹṃ aiṃ aiṃ*, O Independent Yoginī, the great secret residing in the hundred million worlds of Mahātala.

Mūla: On the thighs—Oṃ Auṃ! O Mūla-yoginī, residing in the world of Talātala, you who are the supreme secret of a hundred million [yoginīs]! On the buttocks—Aṃ Aḥ! O Mūla-yoginī, residing in the world of Rasātala, you who are the secret knowledge (*jñāna*) of a hundred million [yoginīs]! In the *mūlādhāra*—Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ! O [you] residing in the world of Pātāla!

*Śatakoṭirahasyatarakriyāyoginī*, the root [syllable] *mū*(0), in the *svādhiṣṭhāna* (*caṃ*(0)), the hundred million most secret *ḍākinīs* residing in the *bhūrloka*. *Mahārasyarākinīyoginī*, the root [syllable] *mū*(0), in the *maṇipūraka* (*ṭaṃ*(0)), the hundred million [deities] residing in the *bhuvarloka*. In the *anāhata* (*taṃ*(0))... [the hundred million]... (4).

In the *viśuddhi* [cakra], at the root of the *lākinī* yoginī, the supreme secret of hundreds of millions of abodes in *svarloka*, is the syllable *paṃ*. In the *ājñā* [cakra], at the root of the *kākinī* yoginī, more secret than the secret of hundreds of millions of abodes in *maharloka*, is the syllable *yaṃ*. In the forehead (*lalāṭa*), at the root of the *sākinī* yoginī, more secret than the secret of hundreds of millions of abodes in *janaloka*, is the syllable *śaṃ*.

O Mūla-devatā, Hākinī Yoginī, who dwells in the Tapoloka and is protected by hundreds of millions; O Laṃ Kṣaṃ, Mahāguptayākinī Yoginī, who dwells in the Brahma-randhra in Satyaloka; together with the Mother Ambā, the foundational power (Ādhāra-śakti), to the Goddess.

*Namaḥ*. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should utter the entire *mātṛkā* and perform the pervasive application (*vyāpaka*) with: "Obeisance to the venerable goddess Parāmbā, who is the form of all the worlds; śauṃḥ hasauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ. Thus it is said.
The venerable Bhuvanyāsa.
Now follows the ritual placement of the forms (mūrtinyāsa).

There, on the head: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ*—salutation to Aṅkeśava and his power, Akṣarā-śakti. On the head. On the mouth: *āṃ*—salutation to Nārāyaṇa and his primordial power, Ādyā-śakti. On the right shoulder: *iṃ*—salutation to Mādhava and his power, Iṣṭadā-śakti. On the left shoulder: *īṃ*—salutation to Govinda and his power, Śāntā-śakti.
On the right side: *uṃ* to Viṣṇu and *uṃ* to Ugrā; on the left side: *ūṃ* to Madhusūdana and *ūṃ* to Ūrdhvanayanā; on the right hip: *ṛṃ* to Trivikrama and *ṛṃ* to Ṛddhi;
on the left hip: *ṝṃ* to Vāmana and *ṝṃ* to Rūpiṇī; on the right thigh: *ḷṃ* to Śrīdhara.

*Oṃ* *luptāyai* *namaḥ*! [On] the left thigh: *ḷṛ* to *Hṛṣīkeśa* and *Lūnadoṣā*. [On] the right knee: *eṃ* to *Padmanābha* and *Ekanāyikā*. [On] the left knee: *aiṃ* to *Dāmodara* and *Kāriṇī*. [On] the right shank: *oṃ* to *Vāsudeva* and *Oghavatī*. [On] the left shank: *auṃ*...
To Saṃkarṣaṇa, [who has] Aurvakā, on the right foot: *aṃ* to Pradyumna, [who has] Añjanaprabhā;
on the left foot: *aḥ* to Aniruddha, [who has] Asthimālādhārā. From the tip of the right foot to the base of the big toe: *kaṃ* to Bhava, [who has] Karabhadrā.
From the tip of the left foot up to the root of the thigh: *khaṃ baṃ* to Śarva and Khagabalā; on the right side: *gaṃ phaṃ* to Rudra and Garimādiphalapradā; on the left side:
*ghaṃ paṃ* to Paśupati and Ghorapādā; at the base of the right arm: *ṅaṃ naṃ* to Ugra.
To Paṅktināsā at the left arm-root: *caṃ* *dhaṃ* to Mahādeva and to Caṃdrārdhadhāriṇī; to the throat: *chaṃ* *daṃ* to Bhīma and to Chaṃdomayī; to the face:
*jaṃ* *thaṃ* to Īśāna and to Jagatsthānā; to the right ear: *jhaṃ* *taṃ* to Tatpuruṣa.

To Jhaṃkṛti (0), on the left ear (6): Ñaṃ ṇaṃ, obeisance to Aghora, the giver of knowledge, and to Ṭaṅkaḍhakvadharā (0). On the forehead (6): Ṭaṃ ḍhaṃ, obeisance to Sadyojāta and to Prakṛtiḍāmāryā (0). On the head (6): Ṭhaṃ ḍaṃ, obeisance to Vāmadeva and to Ṭhaṃprakṛti. In the mūlādhāra (6): Mayaṃ, obeisance to Brahmā.

To Yakṣiṇī, at the Svādhiṣṭhāna: *raṃ* to Prajāpati, *raṃjinī* to [Yakṣiṇī]. At the Maṇipūraka: *laṃ* to Vedhas, *lakṣmī* to [Yakṣiṇī]. At the Anāhata: *vaṃ* to Parameṣṭhin, *vajriṇī* to [Yakṣiṇī]. In the Viśuddha: *śaṃ* to Pitāmaha, *yaśaśidharā* to [Yakṣiṇī]. In the Ājñā: *ṣaṃ* to Vidhātṛ, *ṣaḍādhārālayā* to [Yakṣiṇī].

Having performed the placement [of mantras] as follows: *Arddhendau* (6) *Saṃ* to Viriñci, to the Mistress of All (*Sarvanāyikā*) (0); *Bhālānte* (6) *Haṃ* to the Creator (*Sraṣṭṛ*), to the One with a Smiling Face (*Hasitānanā*) (0); *Nāde* (6) *Laṃ* to the Four-Faced One (*Caturānana*), to the Graceful One (*Lalitā*) (0); *Nādānte* (6) *Kṣaṃ* to Hiraṇyagarbha, salutation to Kṣamā (0). Then: *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hasauṃḥ*.

Having uttered *sahauṃḥ* followed by the entire Mātṛkā, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with: *sakalatrimūrtyātmikāyai śrīparāṃbādevyai namaḥ śauṃḥ hasauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ*. Thus ends the placement of the forms (*mūrtinyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement of mantras (mantranyāsa).
There, in the *mūlādhāra*, [one should offer salutation with]: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ aṃ āṃ iṃ*.

Salutation to the Goddess Ekakūṭeśvaryambā, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of single syllables such as the *praṇava* in its one hundred thousand crore varieties, the bestower of all fruits. In the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: (6) *īṃ uṃ*.

Ūṃ! Salutation to the Goddess Trikūṭeśvarī Ambā, the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of two syllables beginning with Haṃsa, who comprises twenty million times two hundred thousand varieties, and who bestows all fruits. In the Anāhata [cakra]: Ḷṃ Eṃ Aiṃ!
Salutation to the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of four syllables beginning with Candra, who comprises four hundred thousand times ten million varieties.

Salutation to the Goddess Catuḥkūṭeśvaryambā. In Viśuddhi (6): Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ, consisting of the five syllables beginning with Sūrya, comprising five hundred and sixty million divisions, the Sovereign of all Five Peaks (Pañcakūṭeśvarī).
In Ājñā (6): Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ, comprising six hundred and fifty million divisions.

O Lord of all six peaks consisting of the six-syllabled [mantras] beginning with Skanda; O Lord of all seven peaks consisting of the seven-syllabled [mantras] beginning with Gaṇapati, which have seventy million varieties such as *iṃ*, *bi*, *do* (6), *ghaṃ*, *ṅa*, and *caṃ*; O Lord of all eight peaks consisting of the eight-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *chaṃ*, *jaṃ*, and *saṃ*, which have eighty million varieties; O Lord of all nine peaks consisting of the nine-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ṭaṃ*, *ṭhaṃ*, and *ḍaṃ*, which have ninety million varieties; O Lord of all ten peaks consisting of the ten-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *taṃ*, *thaṃ*, and *daṃ*, which have one billion varieties; O Lord of all eleven peaks consisting of the eleven-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *paṃ*, *phaṃ*, and *baṃ*, which have eleven billion varieties; O Lord of all twelve peaks consisting of the twelve-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *bhaṃ*, *maṃ*, and *yaṃ*, which have twelve billion varieties; O Lord of all thirteen peaks consisting of the thirteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *raṃ*, *laṃ*, and *vaṃ*, which have thirteen billion varieties; O Lord of all fourteen peaks consisting of the fourteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *śaṃ*, *ṣaṃ*, and *saṃ*, which have fourteen billion varieties; O Lord of all fifteen peaks consisting of the fifteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *haṃ*, *kṣaṃ*, and *aṃ*, which have fifteen billion varieties; O Lord of all sixteen peaks consisting of the sixteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *kaṃ*, *khaṃ*, and *gaṃ*, which have sixteen billion varieties; O Lord of all seventeen peaks consisting of the seventeen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ghaṃ*, *ṅaṃ*, and *caṃ*, which have seventeen billion varieties; O Lord of all eighteen peaks consisting of the eighteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *chaṃ*, *jaṃ*, and *jhaṃ*, which have eighteen billion varieties; O Lord of all nineteen peaks consisting of the nineteen-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ñaṃ*, *ṭaṃ*, and *ṭhaṃ*, which have nineteen billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty peaks consisting of the twenty-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ḍaṃ*, *ḍhaṃ*, and *ṇaṃ*, which have twenty billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-one peaks consisting of the twenty-one-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *taṃ*, *thaṃ*, and *daṃ*, which have twenty-one billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-two peaks consisting of the twenty-two-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *dhaṃ*, *naṃ*, and *paṃ*, which have twenty-two billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-three peaks consisting of the twenty-three-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *phaṃ*, *baṃ*, and *bhaṃ*, which have twenty-three billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-four peaks consisting of the twenty-four-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *maṃ*, *yaṃ*, and *raṃ*, which have twenty-four billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-five peaks consisting of the twenty-five-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *laṃ*, *vaṃ*, and *śaṃ*, which have twenty-five billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-six peaks consisting of the twenty-six-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ṣaṃ*, *saṃ*, and *haṃ*, which have twenty-six billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-seven peaks consisting of the twenty-seven-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *laṃ*, *kṣaṃ*, and *aṃ*, which have twenty-seven billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-eight peaks consisting of the twenty-eight-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *kaṃ*, *khaṃ*, and *gaṃ*, which have twenty-eight billion varieties; O Lord of all twenty-nine peaks consisting of the twenty-nine-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *ghaṃ*, *ṅaṃ*, and *caṃ*, which have twenty-nine billion varieties; O Lord of all thirty peaks consisting of the thirty-syllabled [mantras] beginning with *chaṃ*, *jaṃ*, and *jhaṃ*, which have thirty billion varieties.

[The Lord of] all [mantras] consisting of the eight syllables beginning with Baṭuka and the eight peaks; in Rodhinī (6), Ñaṃ, Ṭaṃ, and Ṭhaṃ, [the Lord of] all [mantras] consisting of the nine syllables beginning with Brahmā and the nine peaks, which have nine hundred thousand times ten million divisions.

In the *nāda* (6), there are the syllables *ḍaṃ*, *ḍhaṃ*, and *ṇaṃ*; these constitute the entirety of the ten-peaked [mantra] (*daśakūṭeśvara*), which consists of all the ten-syllabled [mantras] beginning with Viṣṇu and comprises ten million times ten million variations. At the end of the *nāda* (6), there are the syllables *taṃ*, *thaṃ*, and *daṃ*; these constitute the entirety of the eleven-peaked [mantra] (*ekādaśakūṭeśvara*), which consists of all the eleven-syllabled [mantras] beginning with Rudra and comprises eleven million times ten million variations.
In Śakti (6): Dhaṃ, Naṃ, Paṃ;

consisting of twelve syllables such as Vāṇī and others, comprising all twelve Kūṭeśvaras with twelve hundred thousand and ten million variations. In Vyāpikā (6): Phaṃ, Ba, Maṃ; [comprising] thirteen hundred thousand and ten million variations.
In the station of *Samanā*,

[there are] the fourteenth-syllable embodiments of Gaurī and others— consisting of all the fourteen peaks (*kūṭeśvara*)— namely *maṃ*, *yaṃ*, and *raṃ*, with fourteen million times one hundred thousand varieties. In *Unmanā*, [there are] the fifteen-syllable variety, *laṃ*, *vaṃ*, and *śaṃ*, with fifteen million times one hundred thousand varieties.
To the sovereign of all fifteen peaks (*kūṭeśvara*) consisting of the fifteen syllables beginning with *Durgā*,
and to the presiding deity of all mantras consisting of sixteen syllables such as Tripurā, including the sixteen varieties of *ṣaṃ*, *saṃ*, *haṃ*, *laṃ*, and *kṣaṃ* within the *dhruvamaṇḍala*.
Salutation to the Goddess Śrī-Ṣoḍaśakūṭeśvarī Ambā, the bestower of all fruits.
Then, having uttered the Kalamātṛkā mantra: *Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hasauṃḥ Śauṃḥ*, [one offers salutation] to the Goddess Śrī-Parāmbā, the presiding deity of all mantras: *Namaḥ Śauṃḥ Hasauṃḥ Śrīṃ*.
One should perform the pervasive placement (vyāpaka) with "hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ. This concludes the mantra-placement (maṃtranyāsa). Now follows the deity-placement (daivatanyāsa).

There, on the right foot: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ aṃ āṃ*—salutation to the goddess Nivṛttyambā, who is served by a thousand crores of families of sages (*ṛṣikulasevitā*). On the left foot: *iṃ īṃ*—salutation to the goddess Pratiṣṭhāmbā, who is served by a thousand crores of families of yoginīs (*yoginīkulasevitā*). On the right ankle: *uṃ ūṃ*.

To Vidyāmbā Devī, served by a multitude of thousands of crores of ascetics—at the left ankle: Ṛṃ Ṝṃ, salutation to Śāntyambā Devī, served by a multitude of thousands of crores of peaceful ones; at the right shank:
Ḷṃ Ḹṃ, salutation to Śāntyatītāmbā Devī, served by a multitude of thousands of crores of sages.
On the left calf: (6) *aiṃ aiṃ* to the Goddess Hṛllekhāmbā, who is served by a multitude of thousands of koṭis of deities.

On the right knee: (6) *oṃ auṃ* to the Goddess Gaganāmbā, who is served by a multitude of thousands of koṭis of Rākṣasas. On the left knee: (6) *aṃ aḥ* to Raktāmbā, who is served by a multitude of thousands of koṭis of Vidyādharas.
To the Goddess Dakṣorau (on the right thigh): *kaṃ khaṃ*, to the Goddess Mahocchuṣmāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the Siddha clan.
To the Goddess Vāmorau (on the left thigh): *gaṃ ghaṃ*, to the Goddess Karālikāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the Sādhya clan.
To the Goddess Dakṣorumūle (at the base of the right thigh): *ṅaṃ caṃ*, to Jayāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of the Apsaras clan.

To the Goddess on the left: *chaṃ jaṃ*, salutation to the Mother Goddess Vijayāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of Gandharva families. To the right side: *jhaṃ ñaṃ*, salutation to the Mother Goddess Ajitāmbā, who is served by a thousand koṭis of Guhya families. To the left side: *ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ*, [salutation] to her who is served by a thousand koṭis of Yakṣa families.
To the goddess Aparāmbā Aparājitā:

at the right breast, *ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ*, to the goddess Vāmāmbā, who is served by a thousand crores of the Kinnara clan; at the left breast, *ṇaṃ taṃ*, to Jyeṣṭhāmbā, who is served by a thousand crores of the Pannaga clan; at the base of the right arm, *thaṃ*.
*Daṃ* on the root of the left arm for Raudryambā, who is served by a family of ten billion ancestors;

*Dha-naṃ* on the right arm for Māyāmbā, who is served by a family of ten billion Gaṇeśvaras; *Paṃ Phaṃ* on the left arm for Kuṇḍalinīambā, who is served by a family of ten billion Bhairavas; *Baṃ Bhaṃ* on the right arm.
To Kālyambā, served by a multitude of a thousand koṭis of *baṭukas*, on the right shoulder: *maṃ yaṃ*.
To Kālarātryambā, served by a multitude of a thousand koṭis of *kṣetreśas*, on the left shoulder: *raṃ laṃ*.
To Bhagavatyambā, served by a multitude of a thousand koṭis of *prathamakulas*, on the right ear: *vaṃ śaṃ*.
To Sarveśvaryambā, served by a thousand koṭis of Brahmā families: *ṣaṃ saṃ* on the left ear.
To Sarvajñāmbā, served by a thousand koṭis of Viṣṇu families: *haṃ laṃ* on the forehead.
To Sarvakartryambā, served by a thousand koṭis of Rudra families: *kṣaṃ* in the *brahmarandhra*.
Salutation to the Mother Goddess Kulaśakti, who is served by thousands of crores of families of moving and non-moving beings.

Then, having uttered the entire Mātṛkā, one should perform the pervasive ritual (vyāpaka) with: "Obeisance to the venerable Parāmbā Devī, the embodiment of all deities; Śauṃḥ Hasauṃḥ Śrī Hrīṃ Aiṃ Oṃ. Thus.
The placement of the deities (daivatanya-nyāsa).
Now follows the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
There, at the *mūlādhāra*, [one should worship] with: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ kaṃ* (0) (4) *anaṃtakoṭibhūcarīkulasahitāyai āṃ kṣāṃ maṅgalāmbādevyai*;
and *āṃ kṣāṃ brahmāṇyambādevyai anaṃtakoṭibhūtakulasahitāya aṃ kṣaṃ*.
To Maṅgalanātha, AṂ KṢAṂ, obeisance to Asitāṅga Bhairava. In the Svādhiṣṭhāna [cakra]:

IṂ LĀṂ, to the Goddess Carcikāmbā Devī together with the host of infinite crores of Khecarīs; IṂ LĀṂ, to the Goddess Māheśvaryambā Devī; IṂ LAṂ, to Carcikanātha together with the host of infinite crores of Vetālas.
*Im laṃ ru ru*, obeisance to Bhairava. In the *maṇipūra* [cakra]:

*ṭaṃ* (four times), to the Goddess Yogeśvarī Ambā, accompanied by the family of infinite crores of Pātālacarīs; *ūṃ hāṃ*, to the Goddess Kaumārī Ambā; [and] to [the one] accompanied by the family of infinite crores of Piśācas, *uṃ haṃ*.
To Yogeśvaranātha, *uṃ haṃ*, and to Caṇḍabhairava, *namaḥ*. In Anāhata: *taṃ* (0) (4).

To the goddess Anaṃtakoṭidikcarī together with her Kula, *ṝṃ sāṃ harasiddhāṃbā devyai*; to the goddess Vaiṣṇavyambā, *ṝṃ sāṃ*; [and] to [the deity] together with the Kula of the infinite millions of those who move in the directions, *ṝṃ saṃ*.

To Harasiddhanātha, Ṛṃ Saṃ, obeisance to Krodhabhairava. In the Viśuddhi [cakra]: (6) Paṃ(0) (4), to the one accompanied by the family of infinite crores of Sahacarīs, Ḷṃ Ṣāṃ, obeisance to Bhaṭṭinyambā Devī;
to Vārāhyambā Devī, accompanied by the family of infinite crores of Brahma-rākṣasas, Ḷṃ Ṣaṃ.

To Bhaṭṭinātha, Ḷṃ Ṣaṃ, obeisance to Unmattabhairava. In the Ājñā [cakra], (6) Yaṃ (3), to the Goddess Śāṃ Kili Kilāmbā together with the Kula of the mountain-dwelling goddesses of infinite crores; to the Goddess Indrāṇyambā, Ai Śāṃ Iṃ.

To Eṃ Śaṃ Kili Kilanātha, accompanied by a host of infinite crores of servants; to Eṃ Śaṃ Kapālabhairava, obeisance! On the forehead: (6) Śaṃ (3). To Auṃ Vāṃ Kālarātryambā Devī, accompanied by a host of infinite crores of forest-dwelling women (vanacarī); to Auṃ Vā Cāmuṇḍāmbā Devī, [accompanied by] infinite crores...

To the one accompanied by the family of *pretas*, Oṃ Vaṃ, to Kālarātrinātha; Oṃ Vaṃ, to Bhāṣaṇabhairava, salutations! In the *brahmarandhra* (6): Laṃ Kṣaṃ, to the one accompanied by the family of infinite crores of *jalacarīs*;
Aḥ Lāṃ, to the goddess Bhīṣaṇāmbā; Aḥ Lāṃ, to the goddess Mahālakṣmyambā.
Oṃ laṃ, homage to Bhīṣaṇanātha, together with infinite crores of the Kūṣmāṇḍa family; oṃ laṃ, homage to Saṃhārabhairava.

Then, one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) with: *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasauṃḥ śauṃḥ aṃ āṃ* (and so on through all fifty-one letters) *samastamātṛkā-bhairavādi-devatāyai śrīparāmbā-devyai namaḥ śauṃḥ hasauṃḥ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ oṃ*. Thus ends the Mātṛkā-nyāsa.
Thus concludes the Great Sixfold Installation (Mahāṣoḍhānyāsa).
The manifold world, the physical form, the mantra, the deity, and the Mothers.
The Mahāṣoḍhā-homa, the Nyāsa, and the Sarvanyāsa are the most excellent among the dark.
Then, having performed the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the hands and the six limbs (kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa) with the previously mentioned mantras beginning with *hasāṃ* and *hasīṃ*,
one should meditate upon the deity as follows:
In the delightful Golden Island arising from the midst of the ocean of nectar.
Within a pavilion of fresh rubies situated in the midst of a forest of wish-fulfilling trees.
Seated upon a lotus on a glorious lion-throne made of the nine precious gems.
Seated within a triangle, possessing the splendor of hundreds of moons and suns. (2)
Adorned with half-moons and arrayed with various ornaments.
Possessing the beauty of ten million Cupids, he was eternally sixteen years of age. (3)
With a gentle smile upon his face, he beheld Bhoja—the three-eyed one with the moon as his crest, adorned with divine garments, garlands, and unguents, and embellished with celestial ornaments. (4)
And [he holds] a drinking vessel, the *cinmudrā*, a trident, and a book in his hands.
For a moment, he bore the splendor of knowledge in the assembly, his face ever-blissful. (5)
It is proclaimed as the Great Ṣoḍhā, served by the entire host of deities.
Thus, one should meditate upon Śiva as Ardhanārīśvara within the lotus of the heart. (6)
O Goddess, one may meditate upon her in male form, or one may contemplate her in female form.
Alternatively, one should meditate upon the partless [Brahman], characterized by existence, consciousness, and bliss. (7)
One should meditate on him as consisting entirely of splendor, possessing a body of both moving and unmoving beings.

Having meditated thus through non-difference from oneself, and having formed the ten mudrās— namely, the yoni, liṅga, dhenu, kapāla, jñāna, triśūla, pustaka, vanamālā, namaskāra, and mahāmudrā— one should meditate on the venerable Guru upon one's head, as follows:

Upon a thousand-petaled lotus, he who possesses the luster of all the cool-rayed moon, whose lotus-hands display the gestures of granting boons and fearlessness, and who is adorned with pure perfumes, flowers, and garments.
O you of serene countenance, for a moment remember the Guru—who embodies all deities—constantly upon your head, preceded by the recitation of his name. (1)
Thus, having meditated upon the glorious Guru.

Having placed that sandal upon his head with the corresponding mantra and having prostrated, he should remember the name given to him by his own guru at his own *mūlādhāra* and meditate upon his own self as being of the nature of Śiva.
Now, the fruit of the Great Sixfold Deposition (mahāṣoḍhānyāsa).
In the Śrīkulārṇava:
O Goddess, when this nyāsa has been performed in this manner, one becomes Paraśiva himself.
There is no doubt that the minister is capable of both punishment and favor in this matter. (1)
Whoever performs the ritual placement (nyāsa) called Mahāṣoḍhā day after day,
All the gods pay homage to him; I bow to him, without a doubt. (2)
Then, the practitioner of mantra should perform the ritual placement (nyāsa) known as the Great Sixfold (mahāṣoḍhā).
This divine field is declared to extend ten yojanas in all directions. (3)
O Goddess, wherever a person goes after performing this nyāsa, [he attains success].
In that regard, there is prosperity, victory, gain, commonality, and a beloved person. (4)
Having performed the Mahāṣoḍhā nyāsa, he pays homage through your initiation.
Even if Śiva himself were to grant a hundred years, one meets with death at the end of those years. (5)
Whoever performs this ritual placement (nyāsa) named Vajrapañjara,
Those dwelling in the heavens, the atmosphere, on the earth, in the mountains, in the water, and in the forests. (6)
Uddaṇḍas, bhūtas, vetālas, devarākṣasas, grahas, and so forth.
O Dear One, with minds seized by fear, they do not look upon the practitioner. (7)
The deities beginning with Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva [perform] this ritual placement (nyāsa) called Mahāṣoḍhā.
All the gods, as well as the sages and the lords of munis, perform [this]. (8)
O Goddess, what is the use of much speaking? One should reveal [this] to a worthy disciple.
One obtains inexhaustible accomplishment; one should perform the ritual placement in secret. (9)
Beyond this, there is no deity more directly bestowing the accomplishment of one's nature.
There is no doubt that this does not exist in the world; it is the truth, the truth, there is no uncertainty. (10)
Entry into the Urdhvāmnāya and the inconceivable state attained through Parā.
The thorough realization of the Great Sixfold [Yoga] is not the fruit of minor austerity. (11)

Having thus performed the Mahāṣoḍhā-nyāsa, if one is endowed with the initiation (dīkṣā) concerning the feet and so forth, one should perform the nyāsa pertaining to that. Therein, first is the Viśrāma-caraṇanyāsa: there, upon the head, having uttered "Oṃ Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Haṃ Saḥ Śivaḥ Hasauṃḥ So'haṃ" and the Turiya-vidyā, [one should recite] "I am the light of existence, consciousness, and bliss" (*saccidānanda-jyotir-aham*).
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haṃ saḥ śivaḥ hasauṃḥ sohaṃ. Having recited the Turiya-vidyā, [I am] indeed the light of existence, consciousness, and bliss. Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ haṃ saḥ śivaḥ hasauṃḥ sohaṃ.
Having recited the Turiya-vidyā, I am indeed the light of existence, consciousness, and bliss. Thus, [the practice of] Caracaraṇa.
Having placed the triad with the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*, rest for a moment.

There, on the head: Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ oṃ yo'ham asmi brahmā vāham asmi so'haṃ svacchaprakāśa-paripūrṇa-parāpara-mahāprakāśa-paripūrṇānandanātha-śrīpādukāṃ.

"I worship; obeisance. Līlānandanātha-Śrī; Saṃbhramānandanātha-Śrī; Citānandanātha-Śrī; Prasannaviśvānandanātha-Śrī. These are the five divine lineages (*divyaugha*) in the Upper Tradition (*ūrdhvāmnāya*). There, on the head: (4) Hrīṃ, I worship the Śrī-pādukā of the Kula-yoginī, the root-vidyā of twenty-five syllables, the Great Siddha of the Kula of both the supreme and the non-supreme, who is filled with pure self-luminosity. (4) Hasauṃḥ, awaken the Self!

The glorious Root Vidyā (mūlavidyāśrī): Haṃ Saḥ, O Supreme Self of the Great Swan (paramahaṃsa-paramātman), Svāhā! "I worship the Śrīpādukā of the Mūlavidyā, the venerable Mahātripurasundarī, whose power is devoid of both void and non-void" (16). Thus, one should place [the mantras] beginning from the feet up to the sixteenfold Vidyā upon the head itself with the Saṃghaṭṭamudrā;
for the Saṃghaṭṭamudrā consists of Śiva and Śakti.
The tips of the four fingers of both the right and left hands, excluding the little fingers, joined together and placed simultaneously facing downwards upon the head;
this is the placement (nyāsa) of the sixteen root-mantras.

Now, if one is endowed with the initiation of the Sixfold Śāmbhava lineage (Ṣaḍanvaya-Śāmbhavadīkṣā), one should perform the ritual placements (nyāsa) as prescribed in the Tantra. They are as follows:
Oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasphreṃ hasauḥ hasakṣamalavaṃrayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ [Śrī] Amukānandanātha hasauḥ hasphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ.

Oṃ, I worship the Śrī-pādukā. Having thus placed the Śrī-guru-pādukā upon the head with the *saṃghaṭa-mudrā* by means of the *guru-pādukā-vidyā* as taught in the *Śāmbhava-tantra*, and having meditated upon it and worshipped it with perfumes and other offerings, [one recites]: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hasphreṃ Hasauḥ Glauṃ Hasauḥ on the right shoulder.
Hasphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Heraṃbāya Namaḥ. On the left shoulder: Aiṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Hasphreṃ Hasauḥ Uṃ Hasauḥ Hasphreṃ Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Aiṃ Durgāyai Namaḥ.
On the right thigh: *baṃ* (five times), obeisance to Baṭukabhairava. On the left thigh: *saṃ* (five times), obeisance to Sarasvatī.

In the heart: (5) *hrīṃ huṃ haṃ kṣaṃ*, by the command of Jvālāmukha-Bhairava, protect, protect me from the flesh-covering! *hūṃ svāhā* (5). Homage to Kṣetrapāla. In the mouth: (5) *paṃ* (5), homage to the Supreme Self (*paramātman*).
Having thus performed the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) and worship, [at the exterior] (5): *oṃ namo bhagavati nīlavajrāsane mama śarīre*.
Rakṣa rakṣa hūṃ phaṭ svāhā. (5) Homage to the seat of the self. Thus, having worshipped one’s own seat.

Having meditated upon the right and left hands as being of the nature of Śiva and Śakti, one should perform the triple *tāla* strike and the binding of the ten directions with the mantra "Sahasraḥ Phaḥ Astrāya Phaṭ," and likewise create a rampart of fire. At the joint of the right index finger and thumb: *hrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. At the joint of the left index finger and thumb...
(5) *ha sa ka la hrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ* | on the right ring finger; (5) *hrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ* | on the left ring finger;

(5) *sa ka lhrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ* | on the left ring finger. Having thus performed the placement (*vinyāsa*), one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) from the head to the feet and from the feet to the head, encapsulated by the five *praṇavas*.
One should perform the placement once with those letters of the Mātṛkā, beginning with 'a' and ending with 'kṣa'. Thus ends the sixfold placement of the seed-syllables (bīja-ṣoḍhā-nyāsa).
Now follows the sixfold deposition (ṣoḍhānyāsa) beginning with Mālinī.
Therein is the first *mālinī* placement (*nyāsa*). At the crest (*śikhā*): (5) *naṃ* to Nādini, (5) *namaḥ*.

On the western face: (5) *ṛ* to Nivṛtti, (5) *namaḥ*. On the northern face: (5) *ṝṃ* to Pratiṣṭhā, (5) *namaḥ*. On the southern face: (5) *ḷṃ* to Vidyā, (5) *namaḥ*. On the eastern face: (5) *ḹṃ* to Śānti, (5) *namaḥ*. On the upper face: (5) *thaṃ*.

To Graṃsinī, salutation! On the two eyes: *dhaṃ* to Priyadarśinī, salutation! On the nose: *īṃ* to Guhyaśakti, salutation! On the upper eye: *caṃ* to Cāmuṇḍā, salutation! On the mouth: *vaṃ* to Vaijriṇī, salutation! On the upper row of teeth on the right: *kaṃ* to Karālī, salutation!

On the upper row of teeth on the left: *khaṃ* to Kapālinī, *namaḥ*. On the upper tusk: *gaṃ* to Śivā, *namaḥ*. On the lower tusk: *ghaṃ* to Ghoṣā, *namaḥ*. On the fang: *vaṃ* to Vīrā, *namaḥ*. On the tongue: *iṃ* to Māyā, *namaḥ*. In the speech: *aṃ*.
Vāgīśvaryai (5) namaḥ. To the two ears: Ṇaṃ Nārāyaṇyai (5) namaḥ. To the cavity of the right ear: U Mohinyai (5) namaḥ. To the cavity of the left ear: Ūṃ Prajñāyai (5) namaḥ. To the throat:
Vaṃ Śikhivāhinyai (5) namaḥ. To the right shoulder: Bhaṃ Bhīṣaṇyai (5) namaḥ. To the left shoulder: [Bhaṃ Bhīṣaṇyai (5) namaḥ].
Or [the mantra] for Vāyuvegā: *namaḥ* (5). On the right arm: *ṅaṃ* Bhīmāyai *namaḥ* (5). On the left arm: *ṭaṃ* Vināyakyai *namaḥ* (5). On the right hand: *ṭhaṃ* Pūrṇāyai *namaḥ* (5).
On the left hand: *laṃ* Śaktyai *namaḥ* (5). On the right thumb: *jhaṃ* Jhaṃkāryai *namaḥ* (5).
*Namaḥ*. On the thumb of the left hand: *ñaṃ* to Kūrdinī, *namaḥ*.
On the staff of the trident in the right hand: *ḍhaṃ* to Kālikā, *namaḥ*. On the staff of the trident in the left hand:
*raṃ* to Dīpinī, *namaḥ*. At the tip of the trident: *jaṃ* to Jayantī, *namaḥ*. In the heart: *paṃ*.

(5) Homage to Pāvanyā! (5) On the abdomen, baṃ laṃbinyai (5) homage! (5) On the navel, kṣaṃ saṃhāriṇyai (5) homage! (5) On the right breast, chaṃ chāgalyai (5) homage! (5) On the left breast, laṃ pūtanāyai (5) homage! (5) Above the right breast, āṃ āmodāyai (5) homage! (5) Above the left breast, saṃ...

To Paramaśakti (5), salutation! To Prāṇa (5), Haṃ Ambāyai (5), salutation! To Citta (5), Aḥ Icchāśakti (5), salutation! To the two buttocks (5), Maṃ Mahākālyai (5), salutation! To the secret place (5), Śaṃ Puṣpāstrāyai (5), salutation! To the semen (5), Aṃ Sūkṣmāyai (5), salutation! To the two thighs (5), Taṃ Tārāyai (5), salutation!

On the right knee: *eṃ* jñānaśaktyai *namaḥ*. On the left knee: *aiṃ* kriyāśaktyai *namaḥ*. On the right calf: *oṃ* gāyatryai *namaḥ*. On the left calf: *auṃ* sāvitryai *namaḥ*. On the right foot: *daṃ* vahnyai *namaḥ*. On the left foot: *phaṃ*.

*Phaṭkāryai* (5) *namaḥ*. *Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasphreṃ hasauḥ naṃ phāṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ*, I worship Mālinī in all the limbs (5) *namaḥ*. Thus one should perform the pervasive placement (*vyāpaka*) upon all the limbs.
This is the Mālinī Nyāsa.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the aggregate of sounds (śabdarāśi).

That [assignment], however, is indeed the previously mentioned assignment of Śrīkaṇṭha and the others; in that case, having omitted the third seed-syllable mentioned there, it should be performed encapsulated by the five *praṇavas*. Therein, it is as follows: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasphreṃ hasauḥ aṃ śrīkaṇṭheśāya pūrṇodaryai hasauḥ hasphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ*, and so forth.
Thus ends the placement of the collection of sounds (śabdarāśinyāsa).
Now follows the placement of the three knowledges (trividyānyāsa).

At the navel: *aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hasphreṃ hasauḥ aiṃ hrīṃ aghore hrīṃ saḥ hasau hasphreṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ aiṃ namaḥ*. At the heart: (5) *paramaghore hūṃ ghorarūpe hasauḥ ghoramukhi bhīṣaṇe vama vama piba rahaḥ heṃ ruru rara hrīṃ hrūṃ phreṃ*.
*Hasauḥ* (5) *namaḥ* | At the center of the brows. *Sphraṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. Thus is the placement of the three Vidyās (*trividyānyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the eight Aghorī goddesses.

There, on the head: (5) *aiṃ hrīṃ ghore hrīṃ saḥ*—salutation to Aghorā. (5) On the forehead: *paramaghore hūṃ*—salutation to Paramaghorā. (5) Between the eyebrows: *ghorarūpe hasau*—salutation to Ghorarūpā. (5) On the mouth: *ghoramukhi saḥ*—salutation to Ghoramukhī. (5) On the throat: *bhīme saḥ*.
(5) Salutation to Bhīmā; (5) at the heart, salutation to Bhīṣaṇā, *saḥ*;
(5) at the belly, salutation to Vamanī, *vamasaḥ*; (5) at the navel, salutation to Pibanī, *pibasaḥ*.
Thus is the ritual placement (*nyāsa*) of the eight Aghorikās.
Now follows the ritual placement of the twelve limbs (dvādaśāṅganyāsa).

Therein: at the two feet, *śreṃ sidhyai* (five times) *namaḥ*; at the two knees, *śreṃ ṛdhyai* (five times) *namaḥ*; at the two thighs, *śreṃ dyutyai* (five times) *namaḥ*; at the private parts, *śreṃ lakṣmyai* (five times) *namaḥ*;
at the navel, *śreṃ kāntyai* (five times) *namaḥ*; at the heart, *śreṃ śivāyai* (five times) *namaḥ*; at the throat, *śreṃ sumukhāyai* (five times).

*Namaḥ*. On the face: *Śreṃ Mālinyai namaḥ*. On the ears: *Śreṃ Nandāyai namaḥ*. On the eyes: *Śreṃ Hayavegāyai namaḥ*. On the forehead: *Śreṃ Mahāmukhāyai namaḥ*. On the head: *Śreṃ Viśveśāyai namaḥ*. Thus ends the twelve-limbed ritual placement (*dvādaśāṅganyāsa*).
Now follows the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).

There, in the heart: *Śrāṃ*, for omniscience, *to the heart, namaḥ*. *Śrīṃ*, O you who possess the flame of nectar-like splendor, *to the head, svāhā*, for eternal satisfaction. *Śrūṃ*, O knower of the Vedas, O primordial awakening, *to the crest-lock, vaṣaṭ*. *Śraiṃ*, to the bearer of the fire-vajra, *svāhā*, for self-sovereignty, *to the armor*.

HŪṂ || ŚRAUṂ, to the one possessing eternal and indestructible power, VAUṢAṬ to the three eyes. ŚRAḤ, to the Pāśupata weapon endowed with infinite power, HŪṂ PHAṬ. PHAṬ to the weapon. Thus is the ritual placement of the six limbs (ṣaḍaṅganyāsa).
It should be performed with that very mudrā. Thus ends the sixfold placement (ṣoḍhānyāsa) beginning with Mālinī.
Now follows the ritual placement of the five great jewels (pañcamahāratnanyāsa).

There, at the *ājñācakra*: (5) *glūṃ gaganaratna gaganapīṭha gaganalokagarbhagāminī gagananāthagaganāṃbā gaganeśvari catuḥṣaṣṭhilakṣakoṭiyoginyaṃbā glūṃ* (5) *śrīpādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ*. At the *viśuddhicakra*: (5) *slūṃ svargaratna svargapīṭha*.

To her who dwells within the womb of the heavenly world, the Mother of the Lord of Heaven, the Mother of Heaven, the Sovereign of Heaven, the Mother of thirty-two million *koṭis* of Yoginīs, *slūṃ* (5), I worship the venerable sandals; obeisance.
(In the Viśuddhi-cakra: [5] *slūṃ*, the heavenly jewel, the heavenly seat, the heavenly world). In the Anāhata-cakra: [5] *mlūṃ*.

O Jewel among mortals, O Seat of mortals, O You who dwell within the womb of the mortal world, O Mistress of mortals, O Mother of mortals, O Sovereign of mortals, O Mother of the sixteen lakhs of koṭis of Yoginīs! *mlūṃ*, I worship the venerable sandals; obeisance. [In the] Maṇipūraka cakra.

*Plūṃ!* O Jewel of the Netherworld (*pātāla-ratna*), O Seat of the Netherworld (*pātāla-pīṭha*), O One who enters the womb of the World of the Netherworld (*pātāla-loka-garbhagāminī*), O Mother of the Netherworld (*pātālāmbā*), O Sovereign of the Netherworld (*pātaleśvarī*), O Mother of the Eight Hundred Thousand Crores of Yoginīs (*aṣṭa-lakṣa-koṭi-yoginyambā*)! *Plūṃ*! (5) I worship the Śrī-pādukā; obeisance! In the wheel of the *svādhiṣṭhāna*: (5) *Nlūṃ!* O Jewel of the Nagas (*nāga-ratna*), O Seat of the Nagas (*nāga-pīṭha*), O World of the Nagas (*nāga-loka*).
Garbhagāminī, Nāganātha, Nāgāmbā, Nāgeśvarī, Turlakṣakoṭiyonyambā, nlūṃ (5), I worship the Śrīpādukā; salutations. Thus is the Nyāsa of the Five Great Jewels.
Now follows the threefold nyāsa beginning with the supreme (parā).

Therein, on the two thumbs: (5) *aiṃ* to Parā, *aiṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the two index fingers: (5) *hraṃ* to Icchā, *hrūṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the two middle fingers: (5) *aiṃ* to Jñānā, *aiṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the two ring fingers: (5) *śrīṃ* to Kriyā, *śrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the two little fingers: (5) *hrīṃ* to Kuṇḍalinī, *hrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ*.
*Phreṃ* to the Mother (*mātṛkā*) *phreṃ*, *namaḥ* on the palm and the back of the hands—thus is the ritual placement on the hands (*karanyāsa*).
Now, one should perform the ritual placement on the six limbs, beginning with the heart, using these same mantras together with their respective seed-syllables (*jāti*).

Then, on the western face: (5) *aiṃ* to Parā, *aiṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the northern face: (5) *hrūṃ* to Icchā, *hrūṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the southern face: (5) *aiṃ* to Jñānā, *aiṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the eastern face: (5) *śrīṃ* to Kriyā, *śrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ*. On the upper face: (5) *hrīṃ* to Kuṇḍalinī, *hrīṃ* (5) *namaḥ*.
*Phreṃ* on the face of Parā (*paravaktre*) (5), *phreṃ* to Mātṛkā (*mātṛkāyai phreṃ*) (5), *namaḥ*. Thus is the threefold nyāsa beginning with Parā.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the lineage of gurus.

There, on the head: (5) *hasakṣamalavarayūṃ sahakṣamalavarayīṃ* [Śrī-]Amukānandanātha Śrīpā[da]. Having thus placed the sandals of one's own Guru with the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*, [place them] in the *brahmarandhra*:
(5) *aḥ haṃ saḥ sohaṃ aḥ śauṃ sauḥ* Jyotiḥ Parāmbā Nirvāṇānandanātha Sauḥ.
ŚAUṂ AḤ SOHAṂ SAḤ AḤ (5). "O Śrīpāda, whose conduct is Nirvāṇa!"—thus one should place [the mantra] with the very *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*.
In the *brahmarandhra* (5): *hasakṣamalavarayūṃ* (*sahakṣamalavarayīṃ*, Śrī-Amukānandanātha 5), Śrī-Parapāvaka, Śrī-pā[dukāṃ]. Thus, one should install [the mantra] with the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*.
In that very place (5): *oṃ hrīṃ kāmadughe amoghe varade vicce sphura sphura śrīṃ śrīṃ* (5).
Kulakāmadhenu Śrīpāda. Then, in that very place, on the right side: (5) HASLAUṂ, the white *nati*, Mahāpīṭha Mahāprakāśānandanātha HASRAUṂ (5), Śuklacaraṇa Śrīpāda. On the left side:
(5) SAHRAUṂ, Raktavidyāmahāpīṭha, Raktapuṣpamahāpīṭha, Raktamaṇḍalamahāpīṭha.
Great seat of the red *caru* offering; great seat of the red lamp; great seat of the red mudrā;

great seat of the red prostration. O Supreme Mother, the Great Illuminator, Śrauṃ (5). [Homage to] the venerable feet of the red one. In the center of the aperture of Brahmā (5), Hasrauṃ Śrauṃ. Great seat of the mixed vidyā.

The great seat of mixed flowers, the great seat of the mixed mandala, the great seat of mixed caru offerings, the great seat of mixed mantras, the great seat of mixed lamps, the great seat of mixed mudrās,
and the great seat of mixed prostrations.

O Great Light, O Great Illuminator! To the feet of the venerable Miśrapāda, the Lord of the Bliss of Equanimity (Sāmarasyānandanātha), ŚrīṂ HASRAUṂ. I worship the venerable sandals of the feet of Miśra. Thus, one should perform the placement with the Saṃghaṭṭa-mudrā.
Thus is the placement of the three feet.
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the three lineages of gurus, beginning with the Divine Current (divyaugha).

There, on the head: (5) *laṃ* obeisance to Brahmā, the great ghost, seated upon a lotus throne; *laṃ* (5) the venerable sandals of Brahmā. In that very place: (5) *vaṃ* obeisance to Viṣṇu, the great ghost, seated upon a lotus throne; *vaṃ* (5) the venerable [sandals] of Viṣṇu. (5) *raṃ* obeisance to Rudra, the great ghost, seated upon a lotus throne; *raṃ* (5) the venerable [sandals] of Rudra. (5) *yaṃ*...

Oṃ *īśvara-mahāpreta-padmāsanāya* namaḥ; *yaṃ*, [seat of] the Great Preta Īśvara, Śrī... | Haṃ *sadāśiva-mahāpreta-padmāsanāya* namaḥ; *haṃ*, [seat of] the Great Preta Sadāśiva, Śrī... | Saṃ *hemagarbha-mahāpreta-padmāsanāya* namaḥ; *saṃ*, [seat of] the Great Preta Hemagarbha, Śrī... | Aiṃ.

Parāyai Aiṃ (5) Parāmbā Śrī (0) | (5) Hrūṃ Icchāyai Hrūṃ Icchāmbā Śrī (0) | (5) Aiṃ Jñānāyai Aiṃ (5) Jñānāmbā Śrīpā (0) | (5) Śrī Kriyāyai Śrīṃ (5) Kriyāmbā Śrīpā (0) | (5) Hrīṃ Kuṇḍalinyai Hrīṃ (5) Kuṇḍalinīmbā Śrīpā (0) | (5) Phreṃ
To Mātṛkā, Phreṃ (5) Mātṛkāmbā Śrīpāda. Thus are the Divyaughas.
Now, the lineage of the Siddhas (siddhaugha):
Āṃ, Ādināthānanda, Ādiparāmbā, Āṃ; [Namaḥ] Śrīpādukāyai. Aṃ, Acintyānandanātha, Acintyaparāmbā, Aṃ; [Namaḥ] Śrīpādukāyai. Aṃ...
Avyaktānandanātha, Avyaktāparāmbā, Kuṃ Śrīpāda;
Kuleśvarānandanātha, Kuleśvarī Parāmbā, Kuṃ Śrīpāda. Thus end the Siddha lineages.
Now, the flood of human beings.
(5) Caṃcaryā-tūṣṇīśānanda-nātha, Siddhāparāmbā, Siṃṭīśāparāmbā, Śrīpāda. (5) Ciñciṇī-mitrīśānanda-nātha, Kubjikāparāmbā, Śrīpāda. (5) Gaganānanda-nātha.
Vāṭulīlāvalī Parāmbā Śrī (5) | (5) Candragarbhānandanātha Balibhāgī Parāmbā Śrī (5) | (5) Muktānandanātha Mahilāparāmbā Śrī (5) | (5) Lalitānandanātha Śaṅkhāparāmbā Karuṇāparāmbā Śrī (5) | (5) Aiṃ ||
Śrīkaṇṭhānandanātha, Śrīkaṇṭhāparāmbā, Śrī (5) || (5) Pareśvarānandanātha, Pareśvarī Parāmbā, Śrī (5) || (5) Kumārānandanātha,
Sahajāparāmbā Ratnādevī Parāmbā, Śrī (5) || (5) Ratnānandanātha, Jñānādevī.

Parāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Brahmānandanātha Nādini Parāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Ajeśānandanātha Mahilāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Pratiṣṭhānandanātha Sahajāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Śivānandanātha Pratibhāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5)
Cidānandanātha, Sahajāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Śrīkaṇṭhānandanātha,
Vidyāśaktiparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Śivānandanātha, Sahajāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Somānandanātha, Sahajāparāmbā Śrī (5) || (5) Saṃvidānandanātha...
Sahajāparāmbā Śrī (5). Vibudhānandanātha Vibudhāparāmbā Śrī (5).
(5) Bhairavānandanātha, Bhairavīparāmbā (5) Śrī(0). (5) Ānandānandanātha, Ānandāparāmbā (5) Śrī(0). (5) Kāmeśvarānandanātha, Kāmeśvarīparāmbā (5) Śrī(0).
(5) Kamalānandanātha, Sahajāparāmbā Śrī(0). Thus ends the three lineages of Gurus.

Having placed [the mantra] at the *brahmarandhra* by means of the *saṃghaṭṭamudrā*, and having again placed the *pādukā* of one's own guru using the *vidyā* of the *gurupādukā* as taught in the *Śāmbhava-prakaraṇa*, one should remember one's own guru— whose name was given by [that] guru— at the *mūlādhāra*.
The placement of the lineage of gurus (gurukrama-nyāsa).
Now follows the ritual placement (nyāsa) of the six lineage-mantras (ṣaḍanvayamantra).

In Ājñā: (5) ŚRAUṂ AIṂ PHREṂ Śrī Parameśvarānandanātha, Pareśvarī Parāmbā (5) Śrī (0). In Viśuddhi: (5) HSRŪṂ (? AIṂ Kubji PhreṂ Śrī Vicceśvarānandanātha, Vicceśvarī Parāmbā (5) Śrī (0). In Anāhata: (5) HSPHREṂ AIṂ.

To Kubjikā, Hsphreṃ Vicce, Haṃseśvarānandanātha, Haṃseśvarīparāmbā (5) Śrī (0). In the Svādhiṣṭhāna (5): Hrāṃ Hrūṃ Hrīṃ Hsrāṃ Hsrāṃ Hsrūṃ Hsrīṃ Kṣrāṃ Kṣrūṃ Kṣrīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Hsphrāṃ Hsphrāṃ Hsprūṃ Hsprīṃ Vicce Hrauṃ.
Hasasaḥspreṃ hasakṣamalavayarūṃ oṃ hasakṣamalavayarīṃ hasakṣamalavayarūṃ hasakṣamalavayarīṃ aiṃ hsrīṃ hsrūṃ hsrāṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ hrāṃ aiṃ nitye bhagavati hsphreṃ kuleśvarī hrāṃ hrūṃ hrīṃ hlāṃ.

hrīṃ hrūṃ hyaiṃ hau ṅa ña ṇa na me kṣrāṃ kṣrūṃ kṣrīṃ kṣraḥ kṣraṃ śrīṃ phaṭ hsrauṃ phreṃ to the fierce-faced Kubjikā, chrāṃ chrūṃ chrīṃ Oterrible One, O Non-terrible One, yaṃ raṃ laṃ va haṃ saṃ kiṇi kiṇi mahākiṇi vicce.

To Saṃvartteśvara Anandanātha and Saṃvartteśvarī Parāmbā, [obeisance] at the Maṇipūraka (5), HṚ SA BRŪṂ AIṂ RIṄGAṬI PIṄGAṬI KAṆṬAPI VICCE; to Dvīpeśvara Anandanātha and Dvīpeśvarī Parāmbā, [obeisance] at the Mūlādhāra (5), HASAKṢAMALAVARAYŪṂ NAMO.

To the Blessed One, Hsphreṃ, to Kubjikā, Hrāṃ Hrūṃ Hrīṃ, Ṅa Ña Ṇa Na Me, O Aghoramukhī, Chrāṃ Chrīṃ Kiṇi Kiṇi Viṇi Viṇi Vicce, Navātmeśvarānandanātha, Navātmeśvarīparāmbā (5) Śrī (0). Thus ends the ritual placement of the mantras of the six lineages (*ṣaḍanvayamantranyāsa*).

Then, having performed the pervasive ritual placement (*vyāpaka-nyāsa*) by means of the root-mantra of the Supreme Lord and the Supreme Goddess, one should meditate upon the Deity in the heart. It is as follows:
Resembling a thousand suns, the Guru possesses great radiance.
The glorious Paraśambhu, the immutable Lord of the six lineages, is the quality of rajas.
O Six-faced One, you are endowed with six throbbing eyes.
His broad hips were girt with a tiger skin, and he was adorned with a garland of severed heads.
He was completely enveloped by a garland of *pārijāta* flowers interspersed with human bones.
With his thumbs joined at the navel of Brahmā, his mouth was wide open with bared fangs.
Adorned with various ornaments, he is the remover of all bonds for those bound by worldly existence.
Holding a trident, sword, spear, and goad, he possesses a massive body.
With his lotus-hands holding a skull, a fruit, a bow, and granting fearlessness,
he sports in the northern Māra forest, surrounded by goddesses in the cemetery.
In this manner, one should meditate upon the Supreme Goddess, resplendent with the weight of her breasts.
Having realized the Śāmbhava state of mind, one should recite the vidyā with undistracted attention.

The visualization of the weapons begins from the upper right hand to the lower right hand, and from the upper left hand to the lower left hand. Having thus meditated and performed worship, one should again practice the two root-mantras and then offer the pair of feet.
