[The mantra: "May Viṣṇu fashion the womb; may Tvaṣṭṛ fashion the forms."

"May Prajāpati fashion [it]; may Dhātṛ pour [the seed]; may he place the embryo within you. Having consecrated it thus, and having recited "Obeisance to Sadāśiva" once while worshipping in the center of the *hetu*, and having worshipped the *tattvas* beginning with "Oṃ, obeisance to Nivṛtti," and having consecrated it twice with the *mātṛkā*, and having consecrated it again with the *mātṛkā*...
Having worshipped [her] with "Sarasvatī Śrī" (0).
Aiṃ! O you who are of unbroken nature, who bring about the bliss of the hand, and whose self is the supreme nectar!
O you who possess a form beyond lineage (akula), place here the spontaneous flash of your own will!
Having thus consecrated it three times with this [mantra].
Klīṃ! O Supreme One, who abides in the Akula, whose form is nectar, and who bestows the knowledge of spiritual accomplishment!
For immortality is deposited within this very reality, which possesses a moist form. (1)
Having thus consecrated it three times with the mantra "sauḥ," [one should offer it] into the arghya vessel which has become one with Your form, O Goddess who are of that very nature.
"Having become the form of supreme nectar, O Amā, cause [the nectar] to vibrate. Having thus consecrated it three times, [one recites]: "Aiṃ Pluṃ Jūṃ Saḥ!
O Amṛte, O Amṛtodbhave, O Amṛteśvarī, O Amṛtavarṣiṇī, cause the nectar to flow, cause it to flow!
Svāhā! Thus [is the mantra of] Amṛteśvarī.

Having consecrated [the vessel] four times with the Vidyā, and having again uttered that [Vidyā]: "Amṛteśvarī Śrī," one should worship it once. Then follows the Dīpanī: *Aiṃ vada vada vāgvādini aiṃ klīṃ klinne kledini kledaya mahākṣobhaṃ kuru kuru klīṃ sauḥ mokṣaṃ kuru kuru sauḥ hsauḥ*. Thus is the Dīpanī.

Having consecrated [the vessel] five times with the Vidyā, and then having recited the Mūlavidyā eight times therein, one should visualize a square with its door facing west in the center; on both sides of that door,
[one should worship] Kulavaṭukanātha and his beloved, or Śrī-Kulagaṇapatinātha and his beloved.
Śrī (0). Having thus worshipped [the deities] on the right and left, and having worshipped the six seats within that as before,

one should invoke the Goddess into the *kāmakalā* situated in the center of the *bindu* within the central triangle by means of the method to be described hereafter, meditate upon her, and perform the application of the six limbs (*ṣaḍaṅganyāsa*).

Having performed the ritual of sakalīkaraṇa and worshipped with perfumes and other offerings, one should worship the dissolution-portion (*layāṅga*) on the limbs of the Goddess according to the procedure to be described; then, having worshipped the lunar-day goddess (*tithinityā*), the sixteen *nityās*, the three lineages of gurus (*gurupaktitraya*), and the six-limbed maidens (*ṣaḍaṅgayuvatī*).
Having offered three or one handful of flowers with the mantra of the Yoginīs in their collective form (samaṣṭi) which is about to be described,
and having presented incense and lamps, [one worships] Yoni, Dhenu, Mahāyoginī, Triśikhā, Padmasaṃkṣobha,
Drāvaṇa, Ākarṣa, Vaśya, Unmāda, Mahāṅkuśa, Khecarī, Bīja, and Yoni.
Having displayed the eighteen mudrās known as the noose, goad, bow, and arrow, one should prostrate with the mudrā of salutation.

If one is unable to perform this much here, one should perform either the consecration (*abhimaṃtraṇa*) or the worship (*pūjana*). If one is unable even for that, having performed the worship of the eight-syllable mantra of the Self (*ātmāṣṭākṣara-pūjā*), and having fully worshipped and gratified the couple Ānandabhairava and Bhairavī, one should begin with the worship of the *kalās* such as Sṛṣṭi and so forth, and complete the remainder.
One should complete it as before.
The ritual procedure for placing the special *argha* offering.
Then, beyond that, one should place another vessel called the *śrīpātra* according to the same procedure;

with it, one should satisfy the deities of the enclosures (*āvaraṇadevatā*) other than the Root Goddess (*mūladevī*). The offering of worship, the dedication of merit, and so forth, as well as the libation (*tarpaṇa*) for the Root Goddess, should be performed with the *viśeṣārghya* alone. In that regard, [the sequence begins with] Anaṅgakusumā and the others.

One should perform the three peripheral coverings (paryanta-āvaraṇa), the offering of worship, and the presentation of the *argha* using only the water from the common *argha*. Thus ends the procedure for the installation of the *śrīpātra*.
Then, in that same sequence, below that, in a row-like arrangement, [one should place] the water for washing the feet (*pādya*) and the water for sipping (*ācamanīya*).
For the purpose of the madhuparka, one should place three vessels according to the very same procedure for the general arghya offering.
If that is not possible, having placed three vessels with their bases upon a triangular mandala,
and having filled two of those vessels with pure water and the third with the liquid of madhuparka,
one should offer a small amount of the special arghya water into them and [recite] the root mantra eight times over each individually.

One should consecrate it with mantras. Regarding the *madhuparka*, a vessel made of *kāśyapa* (wood) is recommended; one should prepare it using either copper or another suitable material, covered by another vessel.
One should place fragrant substances, flowers, unbroken rice, tips of *kuśa* grass, sesame seeds, mustard seeds, and *dūrvā* grass into the general *argha* offering.

One should place eight substances—namely śyāmāka rice, dūrvā grass, kuśa roots, aparājitā flowers, uśīra, and rocanā—into the water-offering vessel (pādyapātra). One should place nutmeg, cloves, and powdered kola fruit into the water for sipping (ācamanīya) vessel. If these aforementioned substances are unavailable, one should place them into the respective vessels while mentally visualizing (bhāvanayā) those very items.
Having poured curds, honey, and clarified butter into the vessel for the *madhuparka*, one should consecrate it with a drop from the special *argha* water.
In the absence of curd and other such items, one should fill [the vessel] with water itself while maintaining the mental visualization of them.

Then, to the right of one's own [seat], one should place the vessel for the *pādya* (water for washing the feet) and so forth according to the prescribed ritual for vessels; furthermore, one should place the vessel for *ācamanīya* (water for sipping) and the *prokṣaṇī* (sprinkling) vessel. Even here, if there is an inability [to do so], one may offer the triad beginning with *pādya* in a single vessel.

Then, having learned the procedure for the ritual application (*viniyoga*) from the mouth of the Guru, one should place the four vessels to the rear of the *prokṣaṇī* vessel according to the rite of the general *argha*. Their names are:
the Guru-vessel, the Śakti-vessel, the Baṭuka-vessel, and the Self-vessel. [One should worship them] with the mantra of the Guru’s sandals (*gurupādukā-vidyā*).
The vessel for the Guru; the vessel for Śakti by means of the *bālavidyā*; the vessel for the *baṭuka* by its own mantra;

and the vessel for the Self (*ātmapātra*) by the eight-syllabled mantra of the Self—one should consecrate each respective vessel eight times with its corresponding mantra. Then, [sprinkle] with the water from the *prokṣaṇī* vessel.
Having taken [the offering] from another vessel, utter *oṃ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ*, the first *kūṭa*, and say:
*ātmatattvātmane namaḥ* | (4) *klīṃ*, the second, and say: *vidyātattvātmane namaḥ* || (4) *sauḥ*, the third, and say: *śivatattvātmane namaḥ* | Then, uttering the whole together: *aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ*.

"Salutation to the Self of all reality. Having thus sprinkled one's own self, one should again sprinkle the sacrificial ground, the sacrificial implements, and the Śrīcakra with the Root Mantra; then, one should display the Dhenu-mudrā over all the objects. This is the procedure for the installation of the Arghya and other offerings.
In this regard, if one is unable to establish the *śrīpātra*, one should perform the aforementioned worship and other rites using only the *viśeṣārghya*.
Now follows the self-worship.
There, having placed a vessel containing the *sādhya* (the object of the rite) upon a triangular mandala in front of oneself,

having filled it with water from the jar and added a drop of the special *arghya*, and having adorned one's own body with sandalwood and other red-colored offerings, while meditating on oneself in the form of the chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*), [one should worship] the Guru and Gaṇapati...

Having prostrated before the Supreme Deity and meditated upon Kuṇḍalinī— from the Mūlādhāra up to the Brahma-randhra— as exceedingly slender as a lotus fiber, possessing the luster of ten million moons and the brilliance of the sun, until the dissolution of the mind, he,
filled with supreme bliss and becoming one with Her, [meditated] upon the Root Mantra from the base upwards.

Having visualized [one's own body] as consisting of light extending up to the *brahmarandhra*, and contemplating one's own body as the form of one's chosen deity (*iṣṭadevatā*) enveloped by that light, one should perform the self-worship (*ātmapūjā*). Then,
having invoked the sixteen digits (*kalā*) of the Moon there, one should [proceed] as before with their names, beginning with [the word] "prāṇa."
It is as follows:

Therein, having conceptualized one's own body as a lion-throne according to the method described in the previously mentioned section on the placement (*nyāsa*) of the yoga-thrones, first, having uttered the *śrī-gurupādukā-vidyā* enriched by the *praṇava* and the three *tārās*, [one says]: "I worship and satiate the venerable *śrī-amukānandanātha-śrīpādukā*."

Having worshipped with "namaḥ" and offered libations, one should worship [the deity] at the *mūlādhāra* with "Gaṃ Gaṇapataye Śrīpādukāṃ Pūjayāmi" and "Tarpaṇam. Having worshipped with "namaḥ" and offered libations, according to the previously mentioned sequence of the *yogapīṭha-nyāsa*,
one should [worship] Maṇḍūka and the others in their respective locations starting from the *mūlādhāra*, using the *praṇava*, the three *tāras*, and the dative case [ending].

Having worshipped that lion-throne with the respective names ending in "namaḥ," one should worship the five *pretāsanas* (seats of the deceased) to be described hereafter on the right shoulder, the left shoulder, the right thigh, the left thigh, and all the limbs. Then, one should worship the fourfold group beginning with Dharma at the locations starting from the right shoulder, and [the remaining deities] at the locations starting from the mouth.
Having likewise worshipped the four beginning with Adharma, and having again worshipped Māyā and Vidye within the heart-lotus, one should meditate on Ananta, endowed with fifteen hoods,
in the center; then, upon the central hood, one should meditate on the eight-petalled lotus, the seat of Kāmeśvarī.
Having worshipped [the deities] beginning with Anantapadma and ending with Paratattva, one should worship in the filaments, starting from the east and proceeding clockwise:
(4) Mohinī Śrī, (4) Kṣobhiṇī Śrī, (4) Vaśinī Śrī, (4) Staṃbhinī Śrī, (4) Ākarṣaṇī Śrī, (4) Drāvaṇī Śrī, (4) Āhlādanī Śrī.

(4) Having worshipped with "Klinnā Śrī," and having worshipped in the center with "I worship the Śrī-pādukā Kledinī," and having worshipped the entire body as the *yogapīṭha* with a handful of flowers using "Klīṃ, obeisance to the lotus-throne of all powers (*sarvaśakti-kamalāsana*"), one should visualize the *śrīcakra* within the pericarp (*karṇikā*) in its center. (4)
Having worshipped the entire body three times with the *vidyā* of the collective (*samaṣṭi*) Yoginīs, beginning with "Samastaprakaṭā" and so forth,

one should worship up to the six seats (*ṣaḍāsana*) in the previously mentioned sequence of the Yoga-pīṭha installation at the locations where they were previously installed, namely: the right shoulder, the back of the right ear, the back of the right temple, and the right [arm].
At the forehead, the right eye, the right nostril, the chin, and the heart—within these five triangles and their centers:
(4) Nāda-śakti Śrī; (4) Bindu-śakti Śrī; (4) Kalā-śakti Śrī; (4) Jyeṣṭhā-śakti Śrī;
(4) Raudrī-śakti Śrī; (4) Vāmā-śakti Śrī; (4) Viṣaghnī-śakti Śrī; (4) Dūtī-śakti Śrī.
(4) Having worshipped with "Obeisance to all the powers of Nanda, Śrī," thus.

Having worshipped all the limbs with the collective seat-mantra (*pīṭhamantra*) as stated in the *nyāsa*— beginning with "Aṃ Kaṃ" (36) and "Śiva-Śakti-Sadāśiva," and so forth— and meditating upon the Goddess in her aforementioned form within the heart-lotus,
one should contemplate one's own body as pervaded by that splendor and as being the very form of the Śrī Bhagavatī, while reciting the root mantra (*mūlamantra*).

Having worshipped [the deity] on the head three times with handfuls of flowers while reciting "Obeisance to Śrī Mahātripurasundarī, O Śrīpādukā," and having gratified [her] with drops of water from the vessel placed in front, one should again, as before, [worship] the head, heart, private parts, both feet, and all the limbs with the root mantra.

Having worshipped and gratified [the deities] with five handfuls of flowers, one should worship the Laya-aṅga-tithi-nityā, the sixteen Nityās, the lineage of Gurus, and the three groups of six-limbed maidens (ṣaḍaṅgayuvatī) in their respective locations within the heart-triangle or the head-triangle, according to the method to be described hereafter.

Having satisfied [the deities], one should worship the powers of the nine enclosures (*navāvaraṇa-śakti*) during the heart-triangle worship according to the method of placement (*nyāsa*) prescribed for the *saṃhāra*-śrīcakra. If it is the head-triangle worship, then after worshipping the powers of the nine enclosures and the Mistress of the Cakra (*cakreśvarī*) according to the sequence of placement for the *sṛṣṭi*-śrīcakra, one should satisfy them. This much [is the procedure].

If one is unable to perform the worship of the Six-Limbed Youthful Goddess (*ṣaḍaṅgayuvatī*), then at the conclusion [of the ritual], having worshipped and satisfied [the deities] three times with the *samaṣṭi-vidyā* beginning with "All Manifest" (*samasta-prakaṭa*) and so forth, one should worship the deities of the four *samayas*, the four *āmnāyas*, and the six *darśanas* according to the sequence of the Śrīcakra worship to be described hereafter. [This concludes the section on] the Upper Tradition (*ūrdhvāmnāya*).

If one is initiated, having meditated upon oneself in the form described in the *Mahāṣāḍhā-nyāsa*, one should worship [the self] three times with its vidyā according to the method to be described hereafter. If capable, one should worship and satiate the deities mentioned in the *Mahāṣoḍhā* at the very locations prescribed for their placement (*nyāsa*), and then [worship] the lineage of gurus of Parā’s feet upon the head.
One should worship the triad.

Then, if one is initiated into the *caraṇa* [tradition], one should worship and offer libations (tarpaṇa) to the previously mentioned *caraṇas* and so forth at the locations of the placement (*nyāsa*) by means of the *vidyās*.

Then, if one has received the full initiation (*pūrṇābhiṣeka*), having worshipped and gratified [the lineage] on the head according to the method to be described— the oral tradition of the *Kāmakalā*— if one is endowed with the silent initiation (*śābdadīkṣā*), one should [place] that group of six couples, that lineage of gurus (*gurukrama*), and that lineage of rays (*raśmikrama*) in the previously mentioned locations for ritual deposition (*nyāsa*).

Having performed worship, one should offer libations. In all these cases of self-worship, if one is unable to perform it in detail, the brief procedure is as follows: having worshipped the respective root deities and the respective lineage of gurus, one should offer them libations.

Then, as before, having offered five handfuls of flowers (puṣpāñjali) upon one's own body at the previously mentioned locations beginning with the entire [body], and having presented incense and lamps, one should perform the internal fire-sacrifice (antarhavana).

There, having visualized a triangular sacrificial pit (kuṇḍa) at the root-support (mūlādhāra), one should contemplate the circle of the fire of consciousness (cidagni-maṇḍala) situated in its center— this being the fire of desire (kāmāgni) which is none other than the fire of time (kālāgni), ignited by the means of latent impressions (vāsanā), fanned by the five vital airs beginning with prāṇa, and presided over by the Supreme Deity in the form of Kuṇḍalinī.

Having meditated upon the *praṇava*, the three *tārās*, and so forth, ending with the root-mantra (*mūlavidyā*), I offer with my mind as the sacrificial ladle (*sruk*) into the fire of the Self—which is kindled by the oblation of merit and demerit—through the path of the *suṣumṇā*, the constant activity of the senses. "I offer this;
Svāhā! Thus, [I offer] the oblation consisting of the mental constructs of what has been done and not done, and of right and wrong action.
Having offered seven oblations with the seven-fold formula, one should then,

beginning with the *praṇava* and the three *tārās*, and ending with the root-vidyā, take hold of the ladle of *unmanī* with the hands of *prakāśa* and *amarśa*, and [offer] the portions of merit and demerit into the full fire.

Having offered the full oblation (pūrṇāhuti) with the words, "I sacrifice; I sacrifice unrighteousness; Svāhā!", the practitioner—having cast aside the entire phenomenal world and having become the form of the partless Brahman—should remain for some moments.
Then, having meditated upon oneself in the form of the Goddess, having bowed to the sandals of the venerable Guru (śrīgurupādukā) at the head,

and having meditated on Annapūrṇā, one should worship and satisfy her with her mantra according to the method of worship to be described; then, [one should take] the water remaining from that worship contained in the vessel, [and offer it to] the sandals of the Guru.
With the thought, "I offer [this] into the mouth of the venerable Supreme Deity, who is the nature of Kuṇḍalinī, by means of the two root-mantras," one should consume [the remainder].

Then, meditating on oneself as being the form of the venerable Supreme Deity, one should perform breath control (prāṇāyāma). Having performed the placement of the seers and so forth (ṛṣyādi), the hand-nyāsa, and the six-limbed nyāsa (kara-ṣaḍaṅga-nyāsa), one should recite the root-mantra one hundred and eight times.
Furthermore, having offered the recitation preceded by breath control (prāṇāyāma), and having praised [the deity], one should prostrate; this is the self-worship (ātmapūjā).
[By Śrīvidyānandanātha, the beloved son of Śiva and Śivā.]
